papers.title: Above-ground biomass recovery after fire in a West African semi-deciduous forest invaded by Cedrela odorata L.
papers.abstract: Abstract Key message Invasion by Cedrela odorata L. can substantially contribute to above-ground biomass recovery after fire while simultaneously altering forest composition. Context Tropical forests are increasingly exposed to successive disturbances that can alter forest dynamics and ecosystem functioning. Understanding long-term responses to disturbances offers a solution for sustainable ecosystem services management. Aims This study assessed the long-term aboveground biomass recovery in a tropical semi-deciduous forest that has undergone silvicultural treatments, devastating fire, and invasion by Cedrela odorata L . We also aimed to quantify the contributions of three species groups: local commercial species (Com), C. odorata (Ced), and non-commercial species (Sec), i.e., all other species. Methods First, we used tree inventory data (diameter at breast height ≥ 10 cm) collected over 42 years from 25 permanent plots covering 100 ha. Then, we used a Bayesian framework to infer the aboveground biomass recovery trajectory. Finally, we analyzed the respective effects of fire severity and silvicultural treatment intensity on above-ground biomass recovery. Results Following invasion by C. odorata, 90% of the biomass lost after the fire will be recovered in less than 50 years. Fire severity affects biomass recovery more than silvicultural treatments. Predictions at the end of recovery indicate a biomass composed of 33% C. odorata , 50% commercial species, and 17% non-commercial species. Conclusion Invasion by C. odorata has advantages and inconveniences for the recovery of forest attributes. These results highlight the importance of adapting forest management strategies to balance ecological resilience and timber production in West Africa, where forest resources are threatened.
papers.summary: Abstract Key message Invasion by Cedrela odorata L. Predictions at the end of recovery indicate a biomass composed of 33% C. These results highlight the importance of adapting forest management strategies to balance ecological resilience and timber production in West Africa, where forest resources are threatened.

papers.title: Heavy Metal Concentrations and Ecological and Human Health Risks in Soils Around Osubi and Aladja Waste Dumpsites, Delta State, Nigeria
papers.journal: IIARD INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF GEOGRAPHY AND ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT
papers.abstract: Open dumping of municipal solid waste can introduce potentially toxic metals into surrounding soils and may create long-term environmental and public-health concerns. This study assessed the concentrations, contamination status, ecological risk and potential human health risks of selected heavy metals in soils around active municipal waste dumpsites at Osubi (Okpe LGA) and Aladja DSC (Udu LGA), Delta State, Nigeria. Soil samples were collected using established field procedures, and cadmium (Cd), lead (Pb), chromium (Cr), nickel (Ni), copper (Cu) and arsenic (As) were determined using Atomic Absorption Spectrophotometry (AAS). Soil contamination and ecological risk were assessed using the geo-accumulation index (Igeo), contamination factor (CF), degree of contamination (Cdeg), modified degree of contamination (mCd), pollution load index (PLI), ecological risk factor (Er) and potential ecological risk index (RI). Pearson correlation analysis was used to examine relationships among the metals, while non-carcinogenic and carcinogenic risks for adults and children were estimated using the hazard quotient (HQ), hazard index (HI) and lifetime cancer risk (LCR). Nickel and arsenic recorded the highest mean concentrations, whereas cadmium had the lowest. Copper and chromium showed a statistically significant positive correlation (r = 0.534, p = 0.049), suggesting a possible common source or similar behaviour in the soil. Although some localized enrichment was observed, particularly for lead and nickel, all Igeo values were negative and classified the soils as practically uncontaminated. The combined contamination and ecological-risk indices also indicated low contamination and low ecological risk. Based on the reported concentrations, HQ and HI values were below 1 for both adults and children, while the estimated cancer risks were below the stated negligible-risk level. Nevertheless, the continued occurrence of arsenic and nickel indicates the need for preventive monitoring and improved waste-management practices. The study recommends routine soil monitoring, improved waste segregation and recycling, engineered landfill development, and stronger enforcement of environmental regulations around the dumpsites.

Copper and chromium showed a statistically significant positive correlation (r = 0.534, p = 0.049), suggesting a possible common source or similar behaviour in the soil. The study recommends routine soil monitoring, improved waste segregation and recycling, engineered landfill development, and stronger enforcement of environmental regulations around the dumpsites.

papers.title: Post-loading Polypoidal Lesion Height and Optical Coherence Tomography Angiography-Defined Regression in Polypoidal Choroidal Vasculopathy
papers.abstract: Purpose: To evaluate the association between post-loading polypoidal lesion height and optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA)-defined regression in treatment-naive eyes with polypoidal choroidal vasculopathy (PCV). Methods: This retrospective cohort study included 51 treatment-naive patients with PCV and a single polypoidal lesion identified on both baseline indocyanine green angiography and OCTA. Patients received three consecutive monthly intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) injections. OCTA-defined regression was defined as the absence of a polypoidal vascular structure on en face OCTA, with flow signals detected in no more than one cross-sectional B-scan slice. Polypoidal lesion height was measured using B-mode optical coherence tomography (OCT). Linear regression analysis adjusted for baseline polypoidal lesion height and receiver operating characteristic curve analysis were performed. Results: During follow-up, polypoidal lesions regressed in 10 (19.6%) eyes and persisted in 41 (80.4%) eyes. The regressed group had a lower polypoidal lesion height than the persistent group (96.8 ± 67.5 μm vs. 232.8 ± 164.7 μm, P = 0.003). After adjustment for baseline lesion height, OCTA-defined regression was associated with a lower post-loading polypoidal lesion height (β = -110.45 μm; 95% confidence interval, -190.27 to -30.63; P = 0.008), and the optimal cutoff was 94.5 μm (area under the curve, 0.806; sensitivity, 80.0%; specificity, 80.0%). Conclusions: Lower post-loading polypoidal lesion height on B-mode OCT was associated with OCTA-defined regression after anti-VEGF loading therapy. Although the identified cutoff requires validation, post-loading polypoidal lesion height may serve as a practical, accessible OCT-based structural biomarker for estimating OCTA-defined regression during routine clinical follow-up.

papers.title: Prediction of the rutting factor of sulfur-modified bitumen using an Aquila-optimized gradient boosting model
papers.abstract: Predicting the rutting factor (RF) of sulfur-modified bitumen from published experiments requires accounting for nonlinear relationships among binder condition, modifier dosage, and aging-related variables while recognizing differences among material systems. This study develops an Aquila Optimization-tuned Gradient Boosting (GBoost-AO) regression model and compares it with XGBoost, Random Forest, support vector regression (SVR), and an Initial-RF identity baseline. The primary analytical dataset contains 221 experimental records from seven published studies. Using five fixed model-selection folds within 185 development records, GBoost-AO achieved a mean coefficient of determination (R 2 ) of 0.8899 and a pooled out-of-fold R 2 of 0.9040. GBoost-AO had the highest mean fold R 2 among the tested configurations, although Random Forest and the identity baseline had lower mean absolute errors. Performance decreased in a retrospective assessment of 36 records from another source study, yielding R 2 = 0.1825. An independent assessment using 23 digitized points from a published 40%-modifier curve yielded a nominal GBoost-AO R 2 of −8.2120 and substantial sensitivity to digitization uncertainty. Direct partial-dependence analysis identified Initial RF as having the largest modeled response range, followed by sulfur/modifier dosage and Aging Type; Sample Age did not affect predictions of the fitted model. Nested assessment across all seven sources also showed source dependence, and a two-record refit shifted the dosage-PDP maximum from 40% to 30%. Favorable development performance therefore coexisted with poor transfer and substantial errors relative to low RF measurements. The study provides a comparative framework for investigating these limitations rather than a validated replacement for binder testing or a general-purpose material-screening tool.

Favorable development performance therefore coexisted with poor transfer and substantial errors relative to low RF measurements.

papers.title: Interphase engineering of carbon fiber/polyimide composites with Nd2O3-modified polyimide sizing for elevated-temperature performance
papers.abstract: An Nd2O3-modified phenylethynyl-terminated polyimide (PI-PEPA) sizing system was developed to regulate the carbon fiber/polyimide (CF/PI) interphase and improve its elevated-temperature interlaminar performance. A two-stage formulation strategy was adopted: the PI-PEPA sizing concentration was first optimized, after which KH560 (γ-glycidoxypropyltrimethoxysilane)-treated Nd2O3 nanoparticles were incorporated at loadings of 0.3–1.0 wt% into the selected 1.0 wt% PI-PEPA formulation. SEM/EDS observations showed a comparatively uniform nanoparticle distribution at 0.3 wt% Nd2O3, whereas increasing nanoparticle loading produced progressively more localized particle-rich regions and coating heterogeneity. XPS confirmed the presence of Nd-containing species on the sized fiber surface, while dynamic contact-angle measurements showed that the apparent surface free energy increased from 50.70 to 55.84 mJ m−2 after incorporation of 0.3 wt% Nd2O3. The same formulation increased the 5% mass-loss temperature of PI-PEPA from 497.05°C to 527.73°C and the residual mass at 800°C from 60.75% to 72.64%. Dynamic mechanical analysis further revealed improved storage-modulus retention at elevated temperatures. The corresponding CF/PI laminate exhibited apparent interlaminar shear strengths of 114.5 MPa at room temperature and 57.6 MPa at 300°C, representing increases of 4.4% and 11.8%, respectively, relative to the PI-PEPA control. These results indicate that 0.3 wt% Nd2O3 provides a favorable balance among surface modification, nanoparticle dispersion, and sizing-layer continuity, whereas excessive loading increases interphase heterogeneity and offsets the benefits of nanoparticle incorporation.

These results indicate that 0.3 wt% Nd2O3 provides a favorable balance among surface modification, nanoparticle dispersion, and sizing-layer continuity, whereas excessive loading increases interphase heterogeneity and offsets the benefits of nanoparticle incorporation.

papers.title: Engineering Pt@β-Cyclodextrin/ZIF-8 Hybrid Thin Films: From Interfacial Surface-Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy to Enhanced Methanol Oxidation Performance in Fuel Cell
papers.abstract: Abstract We report the design, synthesis, and electrocatalytic evaluation of two platinum-containing thin film catalysts for the methanol oxidation reaction (MOR): Pt@β-cyclodextrin (Pt@β-CD) and Pt@β-CD confined within zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (Pt@β-CD/ZIF-8). Both materials were comprehensively characterized by FT-IR, SEM, XRD, Raman spectroscopy, TGA, BET, and AFM. Notably, Pt@β-CD exhibits a previously unreported Pt-induced surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) signature: a broad doublet attributable to Raman-active β-CD-derived interfacial species (including oxidized CD products), supported by synthesis conditions and its suppression after ZIF-8 encapsulation. Zeta-potential measurements (≈ −58 mV) and combined spectroscopic evidence indicate a charge-transfer-mediated chemical enhancement mechanism tied to deprotonated β-CD surface species. papers.title: Near-Infrared Spectroscopic Identification of Ethylene Adsorption States on Ag + -Exchanged ZSM-5 Zeolites
papers.journal: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abstract: Abstract Near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy was applied to investigate the adsorption behavior of ethylene on ZSM-5 zeolites containing Na+, Ag+, and H+ sites. Ethylene adsorbed on Na+ and Ag+ sites could be distinguished by its characteristic NIR absorption band. Further, ethylene adsorbed on Brønsted acid sites was identified by the formation of protonated ethyl species. Temperature-dependent measurements also revealed distinct desorption behaviors associated with different cation sites. The applicability of NIR spectroscopy was further demonstrated by in situ monitoring of ethanol dehydration over Ag+0.5/H+0.5/ZSM-5. Upon ethanol adsorption, ethoxy species were first formed on Brønsted acid sites. At reaction temperatures above 200 °C, ethylene was generated and subsequently adsorbed on Ag+ sites, while water was simultaneously produced. In contrast, the characteristic C–H stretching bands of ethylene were not detected in the mid-IR region under the same reaction conditions. This may lead to the misleading conclusion that ethylene produced during ethanol dehydration is not adsorbed on the catalyst surface. These results demonstrate that NIR spectroscopy provides complementary information to conventional FT-IR measurements for investigating adsorption phenomena and catalytic reactions.

papers.title: The Mix-Match Concept of Digital Supply Chain and Digital Sustainability Practices
papers.journal: International Journal of Environmental Engineering and Development
papers.abstract: The efficient management of global operations and supply chain (SC) flows has become crucial for organisations seeking to achieve operational efficiency, process optimisation, flexibility, and sustainable long-term growth in today's dynamic and linked business environment. This study places a greater emphasis on I4.0 (I4.0) and the technologies it offers, which are particularly beneficial for SC, smart manufacturing and sustainability. I4.0 and its associated technologies, such as the Internet of Things (IoT), big data analytics, cloud computing, and blockchain technology, offer significant benefits for enhancing business optimisation and streamlining labour processes. Enhancing SC networks through the implementation of I4.0 technologies has demonstrated notable improvements, particularly in the field of industrial engineering. Identifying potential risks associated with the process of digitisation is a crucial aspect within an organisational context. The research employed a pragmatic philosophical framework, an inductive methodological approach, and thematic analysis to enhance the quality of the findings. This analysis examines the countries and firms that are at the forefront of global leadership. Additionally, it explores the significance of university partnerships in fostering innovation and driving commercial growth. A digital twin is used for problem-solving purposes, such as network design, decision-making, and the resolution of complicated operational issues. The implementation of organisational strategies can lead to enhanced operational efficiency, reduced risk exposure, and adept responsiveness to market dynamics, so contributing to a more promising future.

papers.title: Size-Controlled and Surface-Modified LDH Nanofillers Enable Multifunctional Transparent PMMA Nanocomposites with Enhanced Thermal Stability and UV Shielding
papers.abstract: Poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA)/layered double hydroxide (LDH) nanocomposites were prepared via emulsion polymerization to investigate the effects of LDH platelet size and surface modification on nanocomposite structure and performance. Size-controlled MgAl-LDH and ZnAl-LDH were synthesized by aqueous co-precipitation, organically modified with various interlayer agents, and incorporated into the PMMA matrix. Structural, morphological, thermal, mechanical, and optical properties were systematically characterized using X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA), scanning and transmission electron microscopy (SEM/TEM), polarized optical microscopy (POM), and UV-visible spectroscopy. The results demonstrated that nanoscale LDH dispersion could be achieved at low filler loadings (1–3 phr), whereas increasing the LDH content to 5 phr promoted significant platelet aggregation. Notably, a high degree of LDH intercalation did not necessarily translate into improved dispersion. Despite exhibiting the greatest interlayer expansion, CDS-modified LDHs showed inferior dispersion and thermal performance, indicating that interfacial compatibility rather than interlayer spacing is the primary factor governing nanocomposite morphology and properties. The optimized PMMA/LDH nanocomposites retained over 85% visible-light transmittance while exhibiting a 27% enhancement in UV-shielding efficiency, improved thermal stability as evidenced by an increased decomposition temperature (T5d), and a higher storage modulus relative to neat PMMA. These findings demonstrate that the synergistic control of LDH platelet size and surface chemistry provides an effective strategy for developing highly dispersed PMMA nanocomposites with simultaneously enhanced optical, thermal, and mechanical properties.

papers.title: A CURE in Oxygen Bomb Calorimetry to Raise Food Awareness and Build Scientific Work Skills
papers.abstract: Abstract In this Course Undergraduate Research Experience (CURE), upper division chemistry and environmental science students in a South Texas public university engaged in a student-driven experiment that allowed them to explore the calorific values (Hg) of different food-derived fuels (e.g., crab shells, fruit peels, wood shavings, artificial sweeteners, herbal teas, and snacks). All student learning objectives (SLOs) were successfully accomplished by enhancing (1) the understanding of the thermodynamics of fuel combustion, (2) the basic and in-depth instrumentation skills in oxygen bomb calorimetry, and (3) the understanding of the scientific method facilitating new research discoveries and training of a qualified workforce in STEM. This one-semester-long pilot study complemented the traditional 2-week-long learning experience in Physical Chemistry foundational courses and brought additional personal gains (attitude, identity, and persistence in STEM) and professional growth (advanced instrumentation, problem solving, and critical thinking). These outcomes were evaluated through student interviews, entry and exit surveys, class discussions, assignments, literature data, and instructor observations. Overall, this CURE was very well received by the students, who addressed meaningful research questions and new hypotheses focusing on food awareness and food waste repurpose for ecofriendly, sustainable agriculture (e.g., wood shavings and fruit peels as “brown” and “green” compost materials for healthy, enriched soils). This laboratory module has high relevance within the context of the current global food crisis and could be easily adaptable to other science curricula such as Food Science, Marine Biology, and Environmental Chemistry.

papers.title: An Intelligent Multi-objective Decision Support Model for Sustainable Remanufacturing
papers.journal: Process Integration and Optimization for Sustainability
papers.abstract: Remanufacturing offers small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) viable pathways towards transitioning to a circular economy; however, intelligent decision-making systems are needed to accelerate its adoption. Balancing the economic, environmental, and social dimensions of sustainability requires the use of analytical tools that can handle multi-dimensional complexity. This study presents a multi-objective optimization model where remanufacturing tasks are allocated to machines in a factory on the basis of minimizing costs, emissions, and noise exposure. Tri-objective optimization has been carried out using the quadrant shrinking method, and Pareto optimal solutions are translated to an implementation framework that can equip SMEs with an intelligent tool for circular economy adoption. In addition to this, we propose an implementation framework for circular economy in manufacturing based on the DMAIC (define, measure, analyze, improve, and control) approach.

papers.title: The transcriptional regulator IκBζ is essential for ILC2 effector functions
papers.abstract: Abstract Group 2 innate lymphoid cells (ILC2) are the sentinels that ensure tissue homeostasis and engage in the immune response to helminths by secreting type 2 cytokines. Here we show that IκBζ, an atypical member of the IκB family, controls basal IL-5 production by ILC2s and governs their effector program during helminth infection and asthma. Peripheral ILC2s express IκBζ at steady state, and its expression is further induced upon stimulation with IL-33 or IL-25 in an NF-κB- and STAT3/5-dependent manner. Upon activation, IκBζ refines chromatin accessibility at regulatory elements of effector cytokine loci, thereby licensing transcription. Due to reduced type 2 cytokine secretion and impaired proliferative capacity of ILC2s, mice with IκBζ-deficient ILC2s show delayed clearance of the hookworm Nippostrongylus brasiliensis and reduced papain-induced airway inflammation. Taken together, our study highlights the central role of IκBζ in orchestrating the ILC2 effector program in different tissues in health and disease.

papers.title: R-PADE: Ranking-Guided Evolutionary Neural Architecture Search forMedical Image Segmentation
papers.abstract: Neural architecture search (NAS) can automate medical image segmentation network design, but costly candidate evaluation limits the supervision available for evolutionary selection. Since replacement decisions depend on relative candidate quality, learning architecture preferences directly can provide guidance under constrained training budgets. In this paper, we propose Ranking-Aware Predictor-Assisted Differential Evolution (R-PADE) for U-Net-style architecture search. Specifically, a predictor trained with pairwise ranking supervision and contrastive regularization directly determines trial–target replacement in discrete differential evolution. Aggregated pairwise preferences prioritize candidates for proxy training, whose observations subsequently update the predictor. This connects evolutionary selection with selective candidate evaluation, reducing reliance on direct training for replacement decisions. Structured encoding and feasibility repair maintain valid architectures during the search. Experiments on CHAOS, BUSI, and ISIC demonstrate competitive segmentation performance with compact architectures. Compared with EU-Net, R-PADE reduces search GPU time by 35.6% while achieving higher Dice scores on CHAOS and BUSI. The ablation experiments compare the implemented predictor formulations and evaluate the contribution of contrastive regularization using matched search settings and proxy-evaluation budgets.

Experiments on CHAOS, BUSI, and ISIC demonstrate competitive segmentation performance with compact architectures. papers.title: Molecular Origins of Solvent Effects in Cyclohexanol Dehydration on H-BEA Zeolite
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract: Abstract Solvents can substantially alter reaction rates by modifying the thermodynamic states of substrates and the free-energy landscapes of elementary steps in acid-catalyzed reactions. Cyclohexanol dehydration within BEA-type zeolite was investigated experimentally and theoretically to elucidate solvent effects on elementary steps. Adsorbed alcohol monomers and dimers were identified in acetone, cyclohexanol, 1,4-dioxane, methanol, and decalin. Hydrated hydronium ions formed in water at Brønsted acid sites (BAS), while solvents interact with protonated cyclohexanol. Kinetic H/D isotope effects (KIE) revealed solvent-dependent rate-determining steps of C–O cleavage (KIE < 2) in acetone, 1,4-dioxane, and decalin, while C–H cleavage (KIE > 2) dominates in water and methanol. Ab initio molecular dynamics simulations showed that acetone induces dissociation of protonated cyclohexanol from BAS to form solvated cyclohexanol-acetone complexes, whereas 1,4-dioxane and decalin leave the alcohol bound to the framework, providing a molecular-level rationale for higher dehydration rates in acetone. Solvation in acetone, 1,4-dioxane, and methanol destabilizes the initial state (excess chemical potential) by 11–13 kJ/mol, compared to 6–7 kJ/mol in water and decalin. The excess chemical potential of the transition state correlates well with the free-energy barrier of the rate-determining step. The excess chemical potential of C–O cleavage transition states in acetone, 1,4-dioxane, and decalin shows greater stabilization (−21 to −11 kJ/mol) than C–H cleavage in water and methanol (−5 to −1 kJ/mol). The combined initial-state and transition-state (de)stabilization yields reaction rates up to 3 orders of magnitude higher in acetone compared to water and decalin.

papers.title: Creatine metabolic network and host immune interplay: from molecular mechanisms to regulatory strategies
papers.abstract: Emerging evidence indicates that creatine, long recognized as an energy buffer in muscle and neural tissues, also plays a critical role in immunometabolic regulation. Research on creatine metabolism and immune regulation spans multiple disciplines, yet a systematic theoretical framework remains lacking. Accordingly, this review proposes a three-dimensional framework of “creatine metabolic flux, immune cell subtype specificity, and microenvironmental regulation”. Beginning with the molecular basis of the creatine metabolic network, we delineate the tissue distribution and functional characteristics of creatine de novo synthesis, transmembrane transport, and the phosphocreatine shuttle. We then analyze, across adaptive immunity, innate immunity, and neuroimmunity, the differential regulatory roles of creatine metabolism in processes including CD8+ T cell antitumor immunity, macrophage polarization, NK cell cytotoxicity, and inflammasome activation. Subsequently, we examine the bidirectional regulatory features of creatine metabolism in the tumor microenvironment and inflammatory microenvironment. Additionally, we synthesize recent advances in creatine metabolism related to anti-infective immunity, vaccine responses, and autoimmune diseases. Throughout, we distinguish direct experimental evidence from correlative observations and explicitly identify the inferential steps that remain to be validated. Through this review, we aim to facilitate a comprehensive understanding of the molecular mechanisms linking creatine metabolism and immune regulation, thereby providing new perspectives for the clinical translation of creatine-based interventions.

papers.title: Cation Valency and Size Govern Thermodynamic Interactions and Nanostructure in Single-Ion Conducting Polymer Blends
papers.abstract: Abstract Understanding how cation valency and ion identity govern the structure and thermodynamics of single-ion conducting polymer blends remains a central challenge in the design of polymer electrolytes. Here, we investigate blends of deuterated poly(ethylene oxide) (dPEO) with poly[3-(methacryloyloxy)propylsulfonyl-1-(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide] containing Na+, K+, Mg2+, and Ca2+ counterions using small-angle neutron scattering (SANS), small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS), and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC). The SANS profiles are quantitatively analyzed using a combination of random phase approximation (RPA) and Lorentzian models to quantify concentration fluctuations and charge correlations. We show that cation valency dictates the dominant structural and thermodynamic behavior: monovalent systems (Na+ and K+) exhibit pronounced concentration fluctuations and systematic composition-dependent structural evolution, whereas divalent systems (Mg2+ and Ca2+) show suppressed concentration fluctuations and more short-ranged charge correlations. At higher compositions of charged polymer, divalent systems further exhibit signatures of phase separation, as evidenced by the emergence of distinct scattering features and multiple glass transition temperatures. These results demonstrate that cation valency primarily governs phase behavior and nanoscale structure, while ion size provides secondary modulation through differences in ion-polymer coordination strength, establishing a direct relationship between cation characteristics, thermodynamic interactions, and nanostructure in charged-neutral polymer blends. Our findings are in agreement with previously developed theory which found that the resulting phase behavior of charged neutral-polymer blends is highly dependent on blend properties such as blend composition, charge concentration and electrostatic strength.

papers.title: Physicochemical Characterization, Compatibility and Stability Assessment of Lenvatinib Mesylate Using Thermal and Liquid Chromatography–Mass Spectrometry Techniques
papers.journal: Analytica—A Journal of Analytical Chemistry and Chemical Analysis
papers.abstract: This study was designed to quantitatively characterize lenvatinib mesylate and assess its compatibility with different excipients used in the preparation of solid, liquid, and advanced drug delivery dosage forms. The excipients evaluated were magnesium stearate, sodium starch glycolate, croscarmellose sodium, pregelatinized starch, microcrystalline cellulose, pluronic acid, stearic acid, and sodium taurocholate. To investigate drug–excipient compatibility, accelerated stability testing, isothermal stress testing, thermogravimetric analysis, differential scanning calorimetry, high-performance liquid chromatography, powder X-ray diffraction, and Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy were employed. Differential scanning calorimetry indicated potential interactions between the drug and magnesium stearate, sodium starch glycolate, pregelatinized starch, pluronic acid, stearic acid, and sodium taurocholate. Isothermal stress-testing studies indicated that the lenvatinib content decreased by no more than 10% in the binary mixtures with magnesium stearate, sodium starch glycolate, croscarmellose sodium, pregelatinized starch, and microcrystalline cellulose after storage at 50 °C. In contrast, the pluronic acid, stearic acid, and sodium taurocholate mixtures showed substantial decreases in drug content, with values of 82.38 ± 0.191%, 83.17 ± 0.108%, and 79.84 ± 0.250%, respectively, indicating potential drug–excipient incompatibility under the investigated conditions. An ion observed at m/z 465.0616 under isothermal stress-testing conditions was assigned as a potassium adduct of the drug ([Lenvatinib + K]+) rather than a separate degradation impurity. These findings provide useful preformulation information for excipient selection in solid, liquid, and advanced drug delivery formulations and support further stability evaluation, degradation product characterization, impurity monitoring, and drug product development.

papers.title: E2F1 signatures stratify immunotherapy response and reveal YWHAQ vulnerability in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma
papers.abstract: To improve biological interpretation of immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) response in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), we developed an E2F1 transcriptional regulation-related framework integrating spatial multi-omics and experimental validation. Single-cell and post-treatment spatial analyses localized E2F1-associated activity predominantly to malignant epithelial states. In ten ESCC Xenium specimens, paired patient-level analyses linked E2F1-high epithelial neighborhoods to lower CD8 effector T-cell and B-cell densities, a lower immune-active niche score, and higher epithelial CD274 -positive fractions. In harmonized public ICI cohorts, E2F1 .Sig functioned as an exploratory response-stratification signature, achieving the highest mean area under the curve (AUC) among evaluated immune signatures across validation and external testing cohorts. Separately, TCGA analyses supported prognostic associations of a 20-gene Hub- E2F1 .Sig risk score. In ESCC, Hub- E2F1 .Sig-based subtyping defined three immune microenvironmental states with distinct survival patterns. Cluster1 showed a more favorable immune contexture and better prognosis, suggesting its association with immune responsiveness. YWHAQ , a key Hub- E2F1 .Sig gene, was associated with poor prognosis, and YWHAQ depletion reduced malignant phenotypes, increased cisplatin-associated apoptosis, and attenuated PD-1/PD-L1-associated immunosuppressive features in vitro and in vivo. Virtual screening identified 6’-Sialyllactose as an in silico candidate YWHAQ-binding compound. These findings support an exploratory E2F1-centered framework and nominate YWHAQ as an ESCC-focused therapeutic hypothesis.

papers.title: Elucidating cancer cachexia–mediated aberrant cardiac wasting signaling in human iPSC-derived cardiac muscle
papers.abstract: Cancer cachexia is a highly debilitating clinical syndrome of involuntary body mass loss featuring profound muscle wasting leading to high mortality. Notably, cardiac wasting is prominent in cancer patients and cancer survivors. Cachexia studies present significant challenges due to the absence of human models and mainly short-term animal studies. To address this translational gap, we have developed a robust human-based cachexia experimental approach characterized by marked cardiac muscle wasting and contractile dysfunction, with increased expression of protein degradation markers. Using human iPSC-derived cardiac muscle, we investigated morphological, functional, and metabolic alterations in the key stages of cachexia and in the post-cachexia phase. C26 and HCT116 tumor cell lines were used to induce cachexia by two methods, pulse addition of cancer cell conditioned media or in transwell-adapted co-culture. Cachectic cardiac myocytes exhibited reduced contraction amplitude, prolonged relaxation time, and increased oxygen consumption rate (OCR), as assessed by video-based and Seahorse analyses. Mechanistic investigations centered on the Atrogin-1/Calcineurin A/NFAT axis revealed this signaling pathway as a central driver of cachexia-induced cardiac atrophy. Cachectic cardiac myocytes exhibited significant upregulation of Atrogin-1, leading to a marked decrease in Calcineurin A protein levels. This, in turn, impaired nuclear translocation of NFAT, thereby suppressing its transcriptional activity and downstream cell growth signaling. These molecular changes were accompanied by increased autophagic flux, as indicated by elevated LC3BII/LC3BI ratios. Furthermore, withdrawal of cachexia-inducing stimuli followed by regular media changes for one week led to normalization of Atrogin-1 and autophagy markers; however, functional impairments and metabolic dysregulation persisted, highlighting delayed recovery. Our new findings establish the Atrogin-1/Calcineurin A/NFAT axis as a key regulatory mechanism in cardiac muscle wasting and suggest this aberrant signaling axis may serve as a targetable mechanism for treatment of cachexia-induced cardiac dysfunction.
papers.summary: Cancer cachexia is a highly debilitating clinical syndrome of involuntary body mass loss featuring profound muscle wasting leading to high mortality. Using human iPSC-derived cardiac muscle, we investigated morphological, functional, and metabolic alterations in the key stages of cachexia and in the post-cachexia phase. Our new findings establish the Atrogin-1/Calcineurin A/NFAT axis as a key regulatory mechanism in cardiac muscle wasting and suggest this aberrant signaling axis may serve as a targetable mechanism for treatment of cachexia-induced cardiac dysfunction.

papers.title: RAD52 is a therapeutic vulnerability for acquired PARP inhibitor resistance in ovarian cancer
papers.abstract: Abstract BRCA -mutated ovarian cancer commonly develops resistance to poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibitors. Here, we investigated the DNA repair protein RAD52 as a potential target to overcome resistance. In analysis of The Cancer Genome Atlas datasets and immunohistochemistry of tissue microarrays, elevated RAD52 expression correlated with poor overall survival in patients with high-grade serous ovarian cancers. We tested two PARP inhibitor-resistant Brca2 -deficient mouse ovarian cancer models, ID8-OR and HGS2-OR. HGS2- OR cells had higher RAD52 expression than parental lines. Rad52 knockout or knockdown restored PARP inhibitor sensitivity in both models. In syngeneic mice, ID8-OR cells in which Rad52 was knocked out yielded lower tumor burden and longer overall survival than control cells. Rad52 depletion impaired single-strand annealing and homologous recombination and led to accumulation of DNA double-strand breaks after PARP inhibitor treatment. RNA sequencing demonstrated that PARP inhibitor treatment induced Polq expression in Brca2 - and Rad52 -deficient cells, suggesting a switch to microhomology-mediated end joining. Finally, the RAD52 inhibitor D-I03 synergized with a PARP inhibitor to reduce cell viability and tumor burden and prolong survival. Collectively, our findings establish RAD52 as a promising therapeutic target to overcome PARP inhibitor resistance in BRCA2 -mutated ovarian cancer and offer mechanistic insights to inform future clinical strategies.

papers.title: α‐tocopherol (Vitamin E) inhibits second mitochondria‐derived activator of caspases (SMAC) mimetic‐induced cell death by directly targeting cIAP1 degradation
papers.abstract: Background and Purpose: Vitamin E is well characterized as a lipophilic antioxidant; however, its non-antioxidant functions remain largely undefined. This study was designed to investigate the non-antioxidant mechanisms by which vitamin E regulates programmed cell death and to identify its specific molecular target. Experimental Approach: A high-throughput screen identified vitamin E as an inhibitor of TNF-α/SMAC mimetic-induced cell death. The mechanism of vitamin E was investigated using western blotting, immunoprecipitation, ubiquitination assays, drug affinity responsive target stability (DARTS), cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA), isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC), and molecular docking. Its in vivo efficacy was evaluated in a murine model of DSS-induced ulcerative colitis (UC). Key Results: Vitamin E selectively inhibits TNF-α/SMAC mimetic-induced cell death by directly and competitively binding to the BIR3 domain of cIAP1. This interaction prevents cIAP1 degradation and the subsequent formation of the RIPK1-dependent death complex, an effect that is independent of its canonical antioxidant function. In a murine model of colitis, vitamin E treatment significantly alleviated disease severity by preserving cIAP1. Conclusion and Implications: Our findings unveil a non-canonical function of vitamin E as a direct cIAPs antagonist and regulator of cell death signaling, presenting a mechanistic basis for its potential therapeutic application in inflammatory pathologies driven by aberrant IAP degradation.

papers.title: Cold gas wind tunnel experiments of a descending launcher first stage and generalization of the engine scaling parameter
papers.abstract: Abstract In the Horizon Europe Project SALTO, a demonstrator of a vertically landing first stage with three Prometheus engines was investigated, the so-called T3. It shall be recovered with a downrange landing approach. In this paper, the results of cold gas experiments are presented where the engine plume was simulated with pressurized air. For that purpose, the engine scaling parameter, which is used to scale the engine parameters and thrust to the experimental conditions, was generalized. It is shown that the matching reduces to a single term, $${\gamma}_{\text{e}}{M}_{\text{e}}^{2}$$ γ e M e 2 . With the parameter in this simplified form, it can be ensured that the relevant similarity parameters for retro-propulsion such as thrust coefficient, momentum flux ratio, and ambient pressure ratio can be matched at the same time. The test campaign showed that switches between the short and the long penetration mode occur for T3, since the re-entry burn is performed at comparatively low thrust coefficients. They cause significant changes of the pressure coefficients on the base area, the short penetration mode giving the lower values, and the lower pressure fluctuations. The transition was quantified from the bow shock stand-off distance extracted from high-speed Schlieren recordings. It exhibits a hysteresis in the thrust coefficient, at Mach 2.0 between C T = 1.896 and 2.905, so that the flow state is not determined by the instantaneous flight condition alone. The upper limit of the long penetration mode decreases monotonically with increasing Mach number, and the mode is confined to a narrow band of angles of attack around zero incidence. Consequences for the design of the flight trajectory are discussed.

papers.title: Wireless sensor network-based real-time monitoring system for large ship airbag launching: design and field validation
papers.abstract: Traditional monitoring solutions for airbag launching of large ships rely on mechanical pressure gauges with limited spatial coverage, slow response times (from several hundred milliseconds to a few seconds), and an inability to monitor dynamically changing attitude parameters during the launching procedure. This paper introduces a WSN-based real-time monitoring solution that combines IMUs and pressure sensors installed at strategic positions on the ship hull and airbags. The solution uses the hierarchical Zigbee mesh with edge computing nodes and the TDMA protocol to deliver real-time, high-speed communication with low end-to-end latency, even under challenging shipyard conditions. The Kalman filter fuses multi-sensor data to provide comprehensive monitoring of pitch, roll, heave displacement, velocity, and acceleration. In-field validation tests have been performed on cargo ships with 1500-2000 DWT capacities during the actual launching process at cooperating shipyards. The system achieves a sampling rate of 100 Hz for inertial data and 50 Hz for pressure data, end-to-end latency under 60 ms (95%), and measurement accuracy of ±0.3° for attitude angles and ±1.5% full scale for pressure measurement. Comparative analysis showed that the proposed system outperforms traditional mechanical gauges with a 75% reduction in spatial blind spots (60%→15% hull coverage), 20–100× faster temporal resolution (50–100 Hz vs. 1–5 Hz), and an 85% reduction in installation time (3.0 h vs. 19.5 h).

papers.title: Advances in computational fluid dynamics for enhanced heat transfer applications in engineering systems: a critical review and comparative synthesis
papers.abstract: Computational Fluid Dynamics has become an important tool for evaluating heat-transfer enhancement in engineering systems where thermal performance must be balanced against pressure loss, energy consumption, and design constraints. This critical review and comparative synthesis examine published CFD investigations of selected heat-exchange applications, including shell-and-tube, double-pipe, twisted-tube, and ground-air heat exchangers. The reviewed studies include nanofluid-based enhancement, geometric modification, internal turbulators, and optimization-based design strategies. The selected literature is compared in terms of evidence for heat-transfer improvement, hydraulic penalties, numerical modeling options, validation methods, and practical applications. The synthesis shows that geometric changes and passive flow-disruption methods can yield significant thermal gains, but at the cost of higher-pressure losses. Nanofluids are also a potential means of further improving heat transfer with relatively minor structural modification, but their long-term stability, fouling characteristics, and pumping needs are still practical issues to be addressed. The comparison also shows that no single enhancement method is always best; performance depends on the exchanger configuration, operating conditions, flow regime, and design objectives. The review highlights the need for consistent thermal–hydraulic performance assessment, better experimental validation, and more attention to manufacturability and long-term operation. It concludes with application-oriented guidance and future priorities for reliable, energy-efficient CFD-assisted thermal-system design.

It concludes with application-oriented guidance and future priorities for reliable, energy-efficient CFD-assisted thermal-system design.

papers.title: CAD-free fine-grained industrial part recognition via 3D Gaussian Splatting
papers.abstract: Abstract Fine-grained industrial parts such as screw, nut, and gear variants differ only in subtle threading, tooth count, or dimensions, and CAD models and large labeled datasets are rarely available in production. We present a CAD-free, video-based recognizer that distinguishes near-identical parts from a single short turntable video per part, with no CAD or manual labels. From the video we reconstruct a 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) twin of each part and render it from 360 viewpoints as a label-free training source. A compact two-layer head, meta-trained over a frozen DINOv2 backbone with a 1-nearest-neighbor (1-NN)-consistent objective, classifies a real part by its most similar reference view. On a self-collected 18-part dataset, evaluated on a separately captured test video from the same rig to control leakage, it reaches 91.6% accuracy from 10 real shots and 75.5% with zero real labels; meta-learning and a strong frozen backbone are both decisive. We compare the renders with the video’s own masked frames, the CAD-free alternative that needs no reconstruction. On the same rig the frames are the stronger source, by 2.4 points at 10 shots and 6.7 points zero-shot with matched view counts, because fine thread relief is not reproduced faithfully. In a hand-held phone capture under different lighting, surface, and viewpoints the order reverses: the renders lead by 11.7 points zero-shot with matched views and by 14 points on nuts, and labeled shots taken on the rig do not transfer. We also report the twin’s reconstruction fidelity, blind zones, and computational cost.

papers.title: FORMULATION AND OPTIMIZATION OF GEMIFLOXACIN-LOADED TRANSDERMAL PATCHES FOR ENHANCED SYSTEMIC BIOAVAILABILITY
authors: Rathlavath Priyanka, I.Nagaraju, K Kishore, G Vijaya Kumar
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This study aimed to formulate and evaluate matrix-type transdermal patches of Gemifloxacin to achieve sustained and effective drug delivery. Preformulation studies, including UV-visible spectroscopy, established the maximum absorption wavelength () of Gemifloxacin at 271 nm, and a standard calibration curve was successfully constructed. Compatibility studies using FTIR and DSC confirmed that the pure drug is compatible with the selected polymers, showing no unexpected chemical interactions or degradation. Nine transdermal patch formulations (F1 to F9) were prepared using varying concentrations of polymers such as Eudragit-L100, Eudragit-S100, and Eudragit RSPO. The prepared patches were evaluated for physicochemical parameters including weight variation, thickness, folding endurance, flatness, and percentage drug content, all of which met acceptable pharmacopeial standards. In vitro diffusion studies demonstrated that drug release is dependent on polymer concentration. Among all formulations, F3 (formulated with Eudragit-L100) emerged as the optimized formulation, successfully passing all evaluation parameters with optimal drug permeation and stability. Zeta potential analysis of the F3 formulation indicated good stability and a smooth surface character. Furthermore, drug release kinetics revealed that the optimized patch followed the zero-order release model. Overall, the study successfully demonstrates the viability of Eudragit-L100 matrix-type transdermal patches for the effective delivery of Gemifloxacin. Keywords: Gemifloxacin and Transdermal drug delivery.

papers.title: Thermal transport and crystallisation in octadecane composites with porous framework coatings and graphene
papers.abstract: Low thermal conductivity and leakage limit the use of organic phase change materials for latent heat storage. Confinement can also delay crystallisation. Polyurea capsules containing n-octadecane were coated with either zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8) or Universitetet i Oslo-66 (UiO-66) and embedded in a polyurethane matrix containing graphene nanoplatelets. Modulated differential scanning calorimetry characterised heat-flow components, while fast scanning calorimetry examined cooling-rate dependence. At a graphene loading of 5 wt%, the ZIF-8-coated composite had an effective thermal conductivity of 0.78 ± 0.04 W m −1 K −1 at 25 °C and an onset-based supercooling of 1.2 ± 0.2 °C. Corresponding values for the UiO-66-coated composite were 0.72 ± 0.03 W m −1 K −1 and 2.4 ± 0.3 °C. Control composites containing only the coating or only the graphene reached 0.31 ± 0.02 and 0.44 ± 0.03 W m −1 K −1 , so neither component accounts for the transport of the complete formulation. The ZIF-8-coated composite retained 98.2 ± 1.1% of its initial melting enthalpy after 1000 cycles between 10 and 60 °C, losing 0.34 ± 0.08% of its mass and showing unchanged infrared and diffraction signatures. Values are means and standard deviations across three independently prepared batches. The two coatings differ in thickness, crystallite size, surface area and growth conditions, so the measurements compare complete formulations rather than isolating a topology-dependent nucleation mechanism. Discharge power at device scale remains untested.

papers.title: An All‐Natural Multifunctional Hydrogel Incorporating Carrier‐Free Self‐Assembled Microparticles for the Treatment of S. aureus ‐Infected Wounds
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Multifunctional wound dressings combining antibacterial activity and tissue regeneration are highly desirable for infected wound management. In this study, a multifunctional chitosan‐gelatin hydrogel incorporating carrier‐free self‐assembled anisaldehyde‐tannic acid‐Zn 2 + (AA‐TA‐Zn 2 + ) bioactive microparticles is developed. These microparticles are fabricated through non‐covalent self‐assembly and metal‐phenolic coordination without additional polymeric carriers or surfactants. Anisaldehyde (AA) serves as both an antibacterial agent and a hydrophobic structural building block, while tannic acid (TA) and Zn 2 + provide complementary antioxidant and coordination functions. Incorporation of these microparticles into the chitosan‐gelatin matrix enhances the structural integrity and multifunctionality of the resulting composite hydrogel through dynamic intermolecular interactions. The hydrogel exhibits excellent injectability, self‐healing capability, tissue adhesion, and sustained release with pH‐responsive behavior. In vitro experiments demonstrate the antibacterial, antioxidant, and anti‐inflammatory activities of the microparticles and composite hydrogel, including their ability to alleviate oxidative stress and inflammatory responses, as well as the hydrogel's effectiveness in disrupting established Staphylococcus aureus biofilms. In a murine model of S. aureus ‐infected wounds, the hydrogel significantly accelerates wound closure and enhances collagen deposition and tissue restoration. This study presents a promising strategy for integrating carrier‐free bioactive microparticles into a natural biopolymer hydrogel matrix, offering a multifunctional platform for infected wound management.

papers.title: Advanced Control Strategies to Enhance Stability of DC Microgrids Islanded under Dynamic Conditions
papers.journal: Iranian Journal of Science and Technology Transactions of Electrical Engineering
papers.abstract: Abstract Islanding of microgrids leads to unwanted fluctuations in power, voltage, current, and frequency parameters. In this paper, a comprehensive three-level control strategy is proposed to stabilize an islanded microgrid by sending control commands to the distributed generation (DG) units based on inverters. The first level of control involves droop control, which manages the power control. The second control level ensures the stability of the voltage and frequency of the network. To implement this control level, the Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) method is used for the DC converter connected to the DG unit, and the Virtual Oscillator Control (VOC) method is employed to control parallel inverters. Finally, the third control level, located at the load side, is responsible for stabilizing the power of the islanded microgrid under varying load conditions, which is implemented using a Shunt Active Power Filter (SAPF) controlled by Model Predictive Control (MPC). Sensitivity analysis of the proposed control model is carried out under transient conditions caused by load variations, environmental changes (changes in irradiance levels), and consequently, changes in the output power of the DG units. Simulation results in the MATLAB/Simulink environment show that the proposed control strategy can stabilize the microgrid and minimize the fluctuations of power, voltage, and frequency under various operating conditions.

papers.title: Ultrasonic Micro Injection Molding of Poly(caprolactone)‐g‐Carbon Nanofibers Synthesized via Surface‐Initiated Polymerization
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Poly(caprolactone)‐grafted‐carbon nanofiber nanocomposites (PCL‐g‐CNF) were successfully synthesized through surface‐initiated ring‐opening polymerization (SI‐ROP) and subsequently processed by ultrasonic microinjection molding (UMIM). Carbon nanofibers were first functionalized with 2‐azidoethanol via [2 + 1] cycloaddition to introduce hydroxyl groups which were used as polymerization initiators. Raman and FTIR spectroscopy confirmed successful functionalization, while the reduced D/G intensity ratio (ID/IG) indicated preservation of the CNF graphitic structure. The extent of functionalization was determined by thermogravimetric analysis and reached a functionalization degree of 9.83 mg of 2‐hydroxyethyl groups per gram of CNF. SI‐ROP of ε‐caprolactone, catalyzed by Sn(Oct)₂, produced PCL‐g‐CNF nanocomposites containing 1, 3, and 5 wt% CNF with yields exceeding 95%. The nanocomposites were extruded, pelletized, and molded by UMIM into tensile specimens. The incorporation of 1 and 3 wt% CNF increased tensile strength by approximately 8% and 15%, respectively, while 5 wt% CNF increased Young's modulus by up to 53%. The thermal properties of the nanocomposites were not significantly affected by CNF incorporation or UMIM processing. These results demonstrate that SI‐ROP combined with UMIM is an effective strategy for producing mechanically reinforced PCL‐g‐CNF nanocomposites with potential applications in the fabrication of medical microdevices.

papers.title: Effects of ultrasound pre-treatment on the physicochemical, structural, thermal, and functional properties of cacauí (Theobroma speciosum Willd. ex Spreng.)
authors: Francisca das Chagas do Amaral Souza
papers.abstract: Abstract The study evaluated the effect of ultrasound pre-treatment on the physicochemical, structural, and functional properties of Theobroma speciosum Willd. ex Spreng (cacauí) seed powder, focusing on the release of bioactive compounds. The proximate composition indicated low moisture content (2.31–3.98%) and high levels of lipids (25.94–28.92%) and carbohydrates (50.31–54.37%), as well as moderate amounts of proteins (14.69–16.25%) and ash (1.78–2.85%), demonstrating high nutritional value. FTIR analysis confirmed the presence of functional groups typical of lipids, proteins, and polysaccharides, showing that ultrasound promoted changes in intermolecular interactions without compromising the chemical integrity of the matrix. The identification of theacrine highlighted the potential of cacauí as a source of bioactive alkaloids of nutraceutical interest. SEM micrographs showed increased roughness, porosity, and particle fragmentation with increasing ultrasound amplitude and time, indicating cell wall disruption and greater exposure of intracellular compounds. Thermogravimetric analysis revealed a thermal profile typical of lignocellulosic biomass, with small variations in thermal stability after treatment. Antioxidant assays (DPPH, ABTS, and FRAP) and total phenolic content showed a significant increase in antioxidant activity, especially under the C70/12 condition, indicating that acoustic cavitation favors the release of phenolic compounds. The mineral profile showed predominance of K, P, Mg, and Ca, as well as Fe, Zn, Mn, and Cu, reinforcing the nutritional potential of cacauí as a source of essential minerals and a functional ingredient.

papers.title: Enhanced electrocatalytic oxygen reduction to H₂O with high selectivity via 2D 1T-MoS₂ integrated with functionalized carbon nanohorns
papers.abstract: Abstract Developing cost-effective and high-performance electrocatalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) is essential for advancing anion-exchange membrane fuel cell technologies. In this study, we report a robust heterostructure formed by covalently functionalized carbon nanohorns (CNH-N) integrated with metallic 1T-MoS₂ 2D nanosheets. Through tailored diazonium chemistry, positively charged ammonium groups were introduced onto CNHs, enabling strong electrostatic and van der Waals interactions with negatively charged exfoliated MoS₂. Structural and spectroscopic analyses confirm successful functionalization, enhanced defect modulation, and intimate CNH–MoS₂ coupling. The resulting CNH-N-MoS₂ catalyst exhibits remarkable ORR performance, including an optimized onset potential of 0.80 V, reduced charge-transfer resistance, and a dominant four-electron reduction pathway with ~ 94% selectivity toward H₂O, which is comparable to commercial Pt/C. These results highlight how controlled chemical functionalization and heterointerface engineering can synergistically enhance catalytic activity and stabilize the 1T-MoS₂ phase. The CNH-N-MoS 2 heterostructures thus represent a promising class of metal-free/low-metal-content electrocatalysts for efficient fuel cell applications.

papers.title: Plant-Derived Hydrolates as Functional Components in Topical Gel and Emulgel Platforms: A Comparative Evaluation of Hydrolate-Based Semisolid Systems
authors: Carla Janaína Rebouças Marques do Rosário
papers.abstract: Abstract Plant-derived hydrolates are aqueous co-products of hydrodistillation that remain underexplored despite their potential as sustainable bioactive ingredients. This study comparatively evaluated two nanostructured topical platforms for hydrolate valoriza-tion: a thermoresponsive nanogel containing Anacardium occidentale L. hydrolate and a nanostructured emulgel containing Pectis brevipedunculata hydrolate associated with babassu oil. Both systems were based on Pluronic F127 and Carbopol 974P and were characterized by physical stability assessment, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, differential scanning calorimetry, scanning electron microscopy, and antimicrobial assays against Escherichia coli , Staphylococcus aureus , and Candida albicans. Hydrolate incorporation influenced the supramolecular organization and biological performance of both platforms, although in a formulation-dependent manner. The A. occidentale hydrolate-loaded nanogel showed thermoresponsive behavior, hydrolate– polymer interactions, reduced crystallinity, compact lamellar morphology, and antimi-crobial activity at the highest tested concentration. The P. brevipedunculata hydrolate-loaded emulgel preserved the structural integrity of the matrix, enhanced hydrogen bonding interactions, displayed a porous amorphous morphology, and improved anti-fungal performance at lower concentration. Overall, these findings indicate that plant-derived hydrolates can act as functional components rather than inert aqueous residues, supporting their use in sustainable nanostructured topical systems with antimicrobial potential.

papers.title: A canopy heat-load threshold for fruiting-site retention and lint yield in long-staple cotton, displaced by trehalose-pathway perturbation
papers.abstract: Heat at flowering cuts lint yield through shedding of squares and young bolls, usually reported as non-transferable abscission percentages. We asked whether fruiting-site survival is a continuous function of canopy heat load, and what displacing it is worth. Sowing date and drip-irrigation interval gave eight environments over two seasons at one southern Xinjiang site, spanning canopy heat loads (HL, hours with canopy temperature ≥ 32 °C in ten days from anthesis) of 17.9–70.9 h. Two long-staple cultivars ( Gossypium barbadense L.) received water, melatonin, trehalose or validamycin A, alongside a source–sink manipulation. Retention of tagged first-position sites declined logistically with HL, with half-retention heat loads of 54.0 h (cluster-bootstrap 95% CI 51.2–57.1) and 70.2 h (66.4–75.1) in the sensitive and tolerant cultivars; leave-one-environment-out error was 0.035 retention units. Lint yield followed boll number, falling 53% in the water-sprayed sensitive cultivar. The benefit of validamycin A grew continuously with HL: at 70.9 h retention rose from 0.109 to 0.293 in the sensitive cultivar and from 0.274 to 0.409 in the tolerant one, whose treated thresholds are extrapolated beyond 70.9 h. Averaged over cultivars in the three hottest environments, it raised retention by 55% and lint yield by 19%, with fibre properties unchanged. Leaf photosynthesis fell only 17%, whereas boll cell-wall invertase activity and sucrose-to-hexose ratio tracked retention within environments, consistent with a sink-side carbohydrate limitation. One site and two seasons establish the form of the response, not its transfer between regions; recalibrated locally, the threshold can inform cultivar, irrigation and spray decisions.

papers.title: Development of chitosan based multifunctional nanostructured systems for cartilage tissue engineering
papers.abstract: In the present work, we report the design and development of multifunctional chitosan (CS)-based hybrid porous nanocomposites (CPIQ I-III) through incorporation of poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) within the CS matrix, followed by functional tagging with magnetite (Fe₃O₄) nanoparticles as a magnetic unit and carbon dots (C-QDs) as a fluorescent unit for cartilage tissue engineering application. The synergistic integration of polymeric and inorganic components enhanced mechanical stability, structural integrity, and antibacterial performance while generating a highly porous architecture that mimics native cartilage extracellular matrix. Among the developed formulations, CPIQ II was selected as the optimized formulation based on an overall assessment of its physicochemical, morphological, mechanical, porosity, antibacterial, and biological properties, rather than mechanical performance alone. The incorporation of Fe₃O₄ nanoparticles and C-QDs further enabled bimodal imaging, facilitating non-invasive visualization and monitoring. In addition, real-time in vitro chondrocyte proliferation and adhesion studies have been conducted to evaluate cytocompatibility and tissue regeneration potential. Overall, this study developed an advanced, multifunctional carbohydrate-based hybrid scaffold capable of supporting cartilage regeneration while enabling simultaneous imaging and healing monitoring, offering a promising platform for next-generation tissue engineering applications.

papers.title: Analysis of interfacial force interaction in the internal polymer flow in the hot end of material extrusion additive manufacturing
papers.journal: The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology
papers.abstract: Abstract To better understand the polymer flow physics through the hot end of a material extrusion additive manufacturing process, a volume of fluid multiphase computational fluid dynamics model (CFD) was formulated to integrate the effect of interfacial forces in the air gap between the heating wall and the melting filament. The model was validated by developing a measurement system that captures the extrusion dynamics, which was quantified in terms of feeding force by using two load cells rated at 5 kg and 20 kg as force sensors and a 1 kg load cell to measure extrudate mass. The CFD experimental validation setup presents a detailed method for integrating an inline force measurement system into a commercial 3D printer, requiring minimal modifications to the printhead and gantry head arrangement. The CFD model result, validated against experimental data, follows more closely the measured feeding force of the 5 kg load cell than the 20 kg load cell. The experimental results further show that lower-rated load cells (5 kg) are more precise at low feeding rates, while higher-rated load cells (20 kg) are better for higher extrusion forces. The CFD analysis of the internal flow through the hot end revealed fascinating actionable insights for exploiting interfacial tension effects for the design of the hot end and extrusion system, enabling faster and more reliable printing. The new understanding of the interaction between thermofluid and interfacial tension can inform process parameter control and the design of desktop 3D printers.

papers.title: Rapid and reliable DNA extraction method for the quantification of X- and Y- chromosome-bearing spermatozoa in ram semen
papers.abstract: Accurate determination of X and Y chromosome-bearing spermatozoa ratios is a useful tool for reproductive management and livestock breeding efficiency. However, the highly condensed chromatin structure of spermatozoa presents a significant challenge for genomic DNA extraction, and current standard protocols are time-consuming. This study aimed to optimise ovine semen DNA extraction for the application of quantifying X and Y chromosome-bearing spermatozoa. A frozen ovine semen sample was divided into four groups (suspension of 30 ×10 6 spermatozoa cells). Three cell lysis methods; 1) 1 h + 10 µL DTT (dithiothreitol) (n = 8), 2) 1 h + 20 µL DTT (n = 7), and 3) 3 h + 20 µL DTT (n = 7), were designed to evaluate the genomic DNA (gDNA) compared to the 24 h + 10 µL of DTT (n = 8) (standard DNA extraction method). Quantitative Polymerase Chain Reaction (qPCR) SYBR Green assay was used to measure gDNA copy number from the extraction group using the housekeeping gene 18S rRNA . The ratio of X and Y chromosome-bearing spermatozoa was assessed using a qPCR TaqMan assay of Y-specific ( SRY ) and X-specific ( PLP ) genes. A gBlock was developed for each 18S rRNA , Y-specific ( SRY ) and X-specific ( PLP ) gene to generate the standard curve of both SYBR Green and TaqMan assays. The reference method of 24 h + 10 µL of DTT yielded the highest copies of extracted gDNA (3,040,919.6 copies ± 2,325,479.6), which was significantly greater than all other methods ( P < 0.05). Meanwhile, Y:X ratio differed significantly among methods ( P < 0.05) by the 24 h + 10 µL DTT and the 1 h + 10 µL DTT treatments yielded comparable Y:X ratios (1.32 ± 0.32 and 1.30 ± 0.21, respectively), indicating no significant difference between these methods. In contrast, 1 h + 20 µL DTT and 3 h + 20 µL DTT resulted in lower Y:X ratios (0.97 ± 0.22 and 0.97 ± 0.17). These findings indicated that the interaction between the DTT concentration and incubation period is critical for releasing spermatozoal DNA. Moreover, the amount of DTT is likely to affect the decondensation of X- and Y-chromosome-bearing spermatozoa differently. In conclusion, optimising the semen DNA extraction method, the 1 h + 10 µL DTT method is less time-consuming and reliable, making it suitable for routine laboratory verification of sperm sex ratio.

papers.title: First contact: biophysical insights into non-enveloped viruses from VLPs to packed virions
papers.abstract: Precise biophysical characterization of non-enveloped viruses and virus-like particles (VLPs) is essential for evaluating assembly, structural integrity, and sample heterogeneity - key parameters that influence infectivity, manufacturability, and therapeutic performance. Analytical ultracentrifugation, light scattering, and mass photometry provide complementary information on particle size distributions, empty/full ratios, and assembly quality. Native and charge-detection mass spectrometry extend this, enabling accurate mass determination and genome-loading assessment. Solution-based structural techniques, such as SAXS and spectroscopy, provide dynamics. High-resolution X-ray crystallography, cryogenic electron microscopy, and tomography reveal global architectures, quaternary arrangements, and conformational switching essential for entry and maturation. Besides these methods, atomic force microscopy also allows nanoscale visualization in conjunction with mechanical profiling, linking physical stability with functional behavior. Thermal, chemical, and mechanical stress assays offer insight into unfolding pathways, pH-dependent disassembly, and genome-driven capsid pressurization, informing both viral biology and formulation science. Finally, mass spectrometry-based methods enable site-specific mapping of post-translational modifications and conformational perturbations. Together, these approaches establish a comprehensive framework for characterizing viral particles and VLPs, supporting rational engineering of stable, homogeneous, and functional assemblies for vaccines, gene delivery, and nanobiotechnology. This review summarizes current label-free methods for assessing size, mass, structural organization, and stability of intact viral particles.
papers.summary: Precise biophysical characterization of non-enveloped viruses and virus-like particles (VLPs) is essential for evaluating assembly, structural integrity, and sample heterogeneity - key parameters that influence infectivity, manufacturability, and therapeutic performance. Besides these methods, atomic force microscopy also allows nanoscale visualization in conjunction with mechanical profiling, linking physical stability with functional behavior. This review summarizes current label-free methods for assessing size, mass, structural organization, and stability of intact viral particles.

papers.title: Simulation of Electron Trapping in Polymer Light-Emitting Diodes
papers.abstract: Abstract Electron trapping in polymer light-emitting diodes (PLEDs) operated at constant voltage results in a decrease of current and light emission over many minutes, and the decline becomes more pronounced with decreasing temperature. This seems to contradict the established electron trap formation scenario, which is temperature-activated and therefore decelerates when cooling down. Numerical simulations are performed on the device characteristics of pristine PLEDs and during operation, i.e., when electron traps form. The experimental current and emission trends are explained by a temperature-dependent variation of the trap occupancy, which is determined by the temperature-dependent charge mobilities and capture rates. Matching the simulated electron trap density between the PLED and the electron-only device requires a very slow electron capture rate, which is reasoned by the specific electron trap formation process in semiconducting polymers.

papers.title: Upcycling cornstalk waste into bio-superabsorbent polymers via graft polymerization of ultrasonically fractionated crude cellulose for agricultural applications
papers.abstract: A cornstalk–derived superabsorbent polymer was prepared by grafting acrylic acid and bio-based itaconic acid, with the synthesis conditions systematically optimized using response surface methodology. Response surface analysis revealed significant linear and quadratic effects of the formulation variables, with a significant interaction between crosslinker concentration and itaconic acid content. Moderate formulation levels provided a favourable balance between network formation and swelling performance, whereas excessive crosslinking and high itaconic acid content decreased water uptake. The cellulose-based superabsorbent polymer exhibited a maximum absorption capacity of 520 g/g in deionized water and a reduced uptake in saline media, reflecting the effect of ionic strength on swelling. Swelling progressively decreased over successive wet–dry cycles, while the material retained substantial swelling capacity after four cycles. Complementary SEM, TGA, solid-state NMR, and XRD analyses were performed to establish structure–property relationships and confirm material integrity.

papers.title: Dynamic heterogeneous graph attention network for spatiotemporal correlation modeling of mine microseismic events and intelligent rockburst risk level reasoning
papers.abstract: Deep mining releases accumulated strain energy violently, and microseismic arrays record the fracturing that precedes rockbursts. Graph neural networks have already been applied to seismic and microseismic tasks such as phase association, source characterisation and event forecasting; what those graphs share is a topology anchored to a fixed sensor array and a single edge semantics, so they cannot follow an event field that turns over as the working face advances. This paper proposes a dynamic heterogeneous graph attention network (DHGAT). Every event enters as a node that retains four feature channels — waveform, source parameter, spatial and temporal — and three edge types (spatial proximity, temporal sequence, feature similarity) are rebuilt inside a 48 h sliding window. Relation-specific multi-head attention aggregates neighbours separately for each edge type, a semantic-level layer learns how much each relation contributes, and a gated recurrent encoder tracks the evolving graph embedding before four risk grades are assigned: no risk, low, moderate and high. On a 24-month catalogue of 7956 events from one deep metal mine, DHGAT reached 91.9 ± 0.4% accuracy, 0.853 ± 0.008 macro-F1 and 0.887 ± 0.006 quadratic weighted Kappa over ten runs, ahead of the strongest static heterogeneous baseline (HAN, 89.2% and 0.788) and of every other baseline at p < 0.01; recall on high-risk events reached 80.0%. Relation weights migrate from spatially dominated during gradual stress build-up to temporally dominated in the final hours before failure, which mirrors the shift from distributed microcracking to localised coalescence, and a perturbation test confirms that the attention carries the discriminative signal. Inference costs 46 ms per window on a single NVIDIA RTX 3090 GPU. All data come from one mine, so the reported thresholds require recalibration before transfer.
papers.summary: Deep mining releases accumulated strain energy violently, and microseismic arrays record the fracturing that precedes rockbursts. Inference costs 46 ms per window on a single NVIDIA RTX 3090 GPU. All data come from one mine, so the reported thresholds require recalibration before transfer.

papers.title: Institutional Embeddedness and Collaborative ESG Governance: Configurational Mechanisms of Green Transformation Among Heavily Polluting Firms in China
papers.journal: American Journal of Economics and Sociology
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Improving ESG governance in heavily polluting firms has become a critical yet insufficiently understood issue. Existing studies predominantly examine the net effects of individual factors, but pay limited attention to the configurational logic through which internal structures and external contexts jointly shape ESG outcomes. Drawing on the structure–context framework, this study integrates NCA and fsQCA to examine the driving mechanisms of ESG governance among 148 A‐share listed heavily polluting firms in China over 2021–2024. The NCA results reveal that shareholder network centrality (DC) and investor sentiment (SS) function as bottleneck‐like lower‐bound conditions for achieving a targeted level of ESG governance. Building on this boundary‐setting insight, the fsQCA results identify three equifinal pathways to high ESG governance: Agile Response–Policy‐Market Resonance, Resource‐Driven–Institutional Embeddedness, and Network Synergy–Low‐Carbon Leadership. In contrast, the configurational pathways leading to non‐high ESG governance are markedly different, confirming causal asymmetry. This study enriches configurational ESG research and provides differentiated strategic implications for the green transformation of heavily polluting firms under the Dual Carbon goals.

The NCA results reveal that shareholder network centrality (DC) and investor sentiment (SS) function as bottleneck‐like lower‐bound conditions for achieving a targeted level of ESG governance. papers.title: Selective catalysis to convert lignin-rich biomass into clean-label vanillin for plant-based dairy and beverages
papers.abstract: The growing demand for soy, pea, oat and other plant-protein matrices to produce dairy and beverage products is driving the need for clean-label vanillin, a natural or nature-identical option that maintains sensory performance and flavor consistency in plant-protein matrices. The global demand for vanilla cannot be satisfied using natural extraction from vanilla orchid pods alone, and catalytic and biotechnological synthesis have become essential, the most important precursor for sustainable vanillin production that does not compete with food use. This review discusses the lignin structure and the yield of vanillin by catalytic routes, such as perovskites, polyoxometalates, metal oxides, LDH-based catalysts, and enzymes, and explores reaction mechanisms, catalyst stability, and industrial feasibility. We believe the key problem in the production of vanillin from food-grade lignin is not only catalytic yield, but also an intractable triangle consisting of vanillin selectivity, the transition metal catalyst residue in the product and compliance with food safety regulations. The most promising path towards industrial use of these systems is a combination of LDH-derived mixed oxides and enzyme-based catalytic systems, and the clean-label plant-based dairy and beverage industry seems to be the testbed for these catalytic systems.
