papers.title: Attention-Derived Dependency Cut for Independent KV-Cache Reuse in Agent Memory
papers.journal: International Journal of Network Dynamics and Intelligence
papers.abstract: Long-term agent memory grows continuously with interaction, making full-memory prefill increasingly costly in terms of time to first token (TTFT) and redundant computation. KV-cache reuse could avoid repeatedly prefilling the accumulated memory, but KV caching relies on exact prefix matching. When memory is updated, reorganized, or assembled from reusable units, prefix mismatches prevent direct reuse of existing KV caches and force the model to recompute a long memory prefix. Existing methods largely assume that memory blocks are already given and address the prefix-matching limitation by concatenating their KV caches and then repairing the resulting mismatch. We therefore argue that the primary question for agent-memory KV reuse is where to segment the memory. We propose AD-CUT, an Attention-derived dependency Cut method for training-free, independence-oriented segmentation. AD-Cut computes attention-derived dependency signals over sentence-level atomic units, including an incoming signal Ain and an outgoing signal Aout, and selects boundaries where both signals are low. The signals exhibit stable positive associations with intervention-derived KV and NLL sensitivity, with Spearman ρ ranging from 0.615 to 0.868 and context-cluster bootstrap intervals remaining positive, supporting their use as predictive proxies. In block-KV serving for agent QA, AD-Cut achieves a 16.17× Online TTFT speedup with a QA Quality Retention of 0.7675. It also improves task quality over naive sentence-level reuse in a controlled agent-memory evaluation. These results show that AD-Cut substantially reduces online computation while mitigating the quality loss caused by KV-cache reuse.
papers.summary: Long-term agent memory grows continuously with interaction, making full-memory prefill increasingly costly in terms of time to first token (TTFT) and redundant computation. Existing methods largely assume that memory blocks are already given and address the prefix-matching limitation by concatenating their KV caches and then repairing the resulting mismatch. These results show that AD-Cut substantially reduces online computation while mitigating the quality loss caused by KV-cache reuse.

papers.title: Quantitative Toxicophore Discovery through Interpretable Deep Learning: A Framework for Mechanism-Guided Toxicity Mitigation in Drug Safety Profiling
papers.abstract: Abstract Unanticipated toxicity accounts for ∼30% of clinical-phase drug failures, yet despite advances in computational toxicity prediction, predictive models typically offer scores without identifying the structural culprit. Here, we introduce an interpretable deep-learning framework that couples fingerprint-descriptor fusion with task-adaptive attention and a SHAP-guided bioisosteric ablation pipeline. Trained on 9,315 compounds spanning 14 end points (Tox21 + ClinTox) under scaffold-stratified split, the attention-fusion model achieves mean test ROC-AUC of 0.739 (Tox21) and 0.953 (ClinTox). The critical advance is a structure-guided validation protocol: predictive intervention ablation─computationally replacing toxicophores with bioisosteric equivalents─demonstrates that the model’s predictions are predictively dependent on specific substructures. Halogen → methyl substitution drops predicted toxicity from 0.659 to 0.101 (paired t = 22.66, p = 6.32 × 10–10, n = 11; Cohen’s d = 6.82), providing the primary structure-guided evidence. Cross-end point SHAP correlation reaches 0.333 (MTL) and 0.334 (STL; Welch’s p = 0.82), indicating that both paradigms extract coherent mechanistic structure above the label baseline (0.172). SMARTS-based toxicophore alignment identifies a strong positive logit differential for aniline on the clinically relevant CT_TOX end point (+0.76), and predictive-intervention ablation confirms model dependence on the identified substructures (halogen → methyl: n = 11, p < 10–9; aniline → methoxy: n = 2, directional check only). External validation on 1,427 SIDER adverse-drug-reaction compounds reveals significant toxicophore enrichment (aniline: 12.6% vs 0%, Fisher exact p = 4.5 × 10–12; halogenated aromatic: 29.8% vs 0%, p = 1.6 × 10–29), remaining significant after controlling for molecular weight and Log P. Three case studies illustrate how SHAP-guided attribution translates into actionable medicinal-chemistry mitigation strategies.

papers.title: Single-cell multi-omics reveals cellular atlases and cell–cell interaction networks in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD)
papers.abstract: Objective To summarize recent advances in single-cell multi-omics technologies in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), with a focus on cellular atlases, cellular heterogeneity, and intercellular communication networks in hepatic and extrahepatic tissues. Methods This narrative review synthesizes findings from studies identified primarily through PubMed searches supplemented by manual curation of reference lists. Search terms included “single-cell,” “spatial transcriptomics,” “MASLD,” “NAFLD,” “NASH,” “MASH,” “steatohepatitis,” and “liver fibrosis.” Studies applying single-cell transcriptomics, single-nucleus RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, single-cell eQTL analysis, and integrative multi-omics approaches were included. The last literature search was conducted in July 2026. Results: Single-cell technologies have revealed key cellular alterations during MASLD progression, including disrupted hepatocyte metabolic zonation, heterogeneous activation states of hepatic stellate cells, macrophage functional reprogramming, immune cell dysfunction, and dynamic remodeling of the hepatic microenvironment. Spatial transcriptomics has further resolved the spatial organization of these cellular changes, whereas single-cell eQTL analyses have linked genetic susceptibility loci to cell-specific regulatory programs. Single-cell profiling of intestinal, adipose, and vascular tissues has expanded the understanding of extrahepatic contributions and gut–liver communication in MASLD. These advances provide a foundation for drug target identification, mechanistic understanding of current and investigational therapies, and assessment of treatment response at cellular resolution. Conclusion Single-cell multi-omics is transforming MASLD research from tissue-level characterization toward cellular-resolution understanding, providing novel insights into disease stratification, therapeutic target discovery, and biomarker development, and advancing precision hepatology.

papers.title: Electric Field Assisted Through‐Thickness Alignment of Carboxyl Functionalized Graphene in Glass Fiber/Epoxy Laminates: Emphasizing Bending, Interlaminar Shear and Fracture Behavior
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT A possible way to enhance the Z‐directional mechanical characteristics of laminated GFRP composites is by suitable through‐thickness alignment of secondary reinforcements. In this work, efficient alignment of polar carboxyl functionalized graphene (FG) in a laminated GFRP composite has been achieved by optimizing the applied z‐directional A.C. field strength. The laminate AF300, where the field strength is 300 V/mm exhibited the best flexural strength among all the composites considered, which is 17% and 32% higher over randomly oriented FG embedded GFRP (RF) and neat GFRP composites respectively. Dynamic mechanical analysis also suggests similar effect where the storage modulus of AF300 composite was found to be significantly better over both RF and Neat composites. Short beam strength as obtained indicates efficient restriction towards delamination due to the through‐thickness alignment of FG. A substantial improvement in energy absorption during Mode I inter laminar fracture toughness (ILFT) test has been noticed due to alignment of FG in the GFRP composite. Similarly, AF300 composite exhibited 84% better Mode II ILFT over the neat composite. Through thickness electrical conductance of AF300 composite is 350% better than Neat and 80% better then RF composite, indicating successful alignment of FG along through thickness direction.

papers.title: Sheng-Jiang Powder and Akkermansia muciniphila interventions in experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis: microbiota-linked sphingolipid/S1PR1-associated barrier remodeling
papers.abstract: Background Sheng-Jiang Powder (SJP) is a classical traditional Chinese medicine formula with reported anti-inflammatory and gut microbiota-modulating activities. However, whether its protective effects in experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) are associated with gut microbial changes, sphingolipid/S1P metabolism, and S1PR1-related barrier signaling remains unclear. Methods EAE was induced in female C57BL/6 mice, with SJP, Akkermansia muciniphila (AKK intervention group), or their combination administered from day 2 after immunization, before the expected onset of clinical signs. Clinical severity, histopathology, inflammatory cytokines, and barrier-related markers were evaluated. Gut microbiota changes were assessed by fluorescence in situ hybridization and 16S rRNA sequencing. Untargeted serum and fecal metabolomic profiles were analyzed by LC–MS. Serum-detected SJP-related compounds were characterized by UPLC–MS/MS and analyzed using network pharmacology. S1PR1-associated signaling was further examined by Western blotting, immunofluorescence, and S1PR1-overexpression experiments in bEnd.3 cells. Results Pre-onset SJP, AKK, and AKK_SJP interventions reduced EAE severity, inflammatory pathology, and serum inflammatory cytokine levels. These effects were accompanied by improved colonic barrier markers, increased Akkermansia -associated mucosal signals, and altered gut microbial profiles. Serum and fecal metabolomic analyses highlighted lipid-related pathways, particularly sphingolipid metabolism and signaling. Serum-detected SJP-related compounds mapped to a candidate network containing S1PR1. In colon and CNS tissues, treatment altered barrier-related markers and S1PR1 expression. In bEnd.3 cells, S1PR1 overexpression reduced ZO-1 expression, whereas SJP-containing serum partially attenuated this change. Conclusions Pre-onset SJP administration alleviated EAE and was accompanied by changes in gut microbial composition, sphingolipid/S1P-related metabolism, S1PR1 expression, and barrier-related markers. AKK-related intervention showed overlapping effects on several microbial, metabolic, and barrier-associated markers.

Results Pre-onset SJP, AKK, and AKK_SJP interventions reduced EAE severity, inflammatory pathology, and serum inflammatory cytokine levels. AKK-related intervention showed overlapping effects on several microbial, metabolic, and barrier-associated markers.

papers.title: Biobased poly(butadiene‐ co ‐myrcene) elastomers reinforced with treated sargassum: tailoring filler–rubber interactions through myrcene content
papers.abstract: Abstract Poly(butadiene‐ co ‐myrcene) elastomeric composites were developed using treated sargassum particles as a bio‐filler (TS), while maintaining constant low silica and silane loadings. This dual marine‐ and plant‐derived design simultaneously valorizes β ‐myrcene as a plant‐derived comonomer and invasive sargassum biomass as a marine‐derived filler. The effects of myrcene composition and TS loading on vulcanization behavior, filler‐network response, morphology, mechanical properties, crosslink density, thermal stability, and viscoelastic behavior were investigated. Increasing myrcene content generally reduced rheometric torque, cure rate, crosslink density, hardness, and stiffness, while prolonging scorch and optimum cure times and increasing network extensibility. The effect of TS on cure kinetics depended on rubber composition and filler loading and was accompanied by increased reversion relative to the corresponding references without TS. Payne effect analysis showed a lower strain‐dependent filler‐network contribution with increasing myrcene composition, although changes in matrix stiffness and crosslink density also contributed to this response. Dynamic mechanical analysis showed that TS increased storage modulus in the biobased rubber composites with TS at appropriate loadings without substantial changes in glass transition temperature. TS also increased Young's modulus, hardness, and elongation at break, but did not systematically improve tensile strength and reduced crosslink density at higher myrcene compositions and TS loadings. Scanning electron microscopy indicated adequate physical contact at moderate TS loading but not conclusive evidence of improved filler dispersion. Overall, β ‐myrcene composition and TS loading provide complementary methods for modifying the stiffness, extensibility, filler‐network response, and viscoelastic behavior of these biobased rubber composites. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

papers.title: Sustainable hybrid activated carbon from banana peel and olive pomace for efficient removal of structurally diverse dyes
papers.abstract: Introduction Agricultural-waste-derived activated carbons offer a sustainable alternative to conventional adsorbents; however, most studies rely on single biomass precursors and evaluate adsorption using only one model pollutant. Methods In this study, a hybrid activated carbon (HAC) derived from banana peel and olive pomace was developed and evaluated for the removal of four structurally distinct dyes: methylene blue (MB), methyl orange (MO), crystal violet (CV), and Eriochrome Black T (EBT). The effects of adsorbent dosage, pH, and contact time were investigated, followed by adsorption isotherm, kinetic, and regeneration analyses. Results An adsorbent dosage of 12 g/L and pH 2 provided the most favorable adsorption conditions. The hybrid activated carbon was found to have a high removal efficiency of 97.71% for MB, 98.41% for MO, 98.70% for CV, and 98.95% for EBT, respectively, under the optimized conditions to remove different dyes with different chemical structures. The equilibrium data were generally better described by the Langmuir model, while the adsorption kinetics showed stronger agreement with the pseudo-second-order model. HAC exhibited maximum adsorption capacities of 130.34, 99.70, 112.42, and 114.52 mg/g for MO, MB, CV, and EBT, respectively, with hybridization enhancing the adsorption capacities toward MO and EBT compared with the individual activated carbons. Regeneration experiments showed that HAC retained adsorption functionality after ten cycles, although removal efficiencies decreased to approximately 42%–56%. Discussion The results in this study validate the potential of olive pomace and banana peel-based hybrid activated carbon as a waste derived, reusable material for the removal of dyes from contaminated wastewater, thereby valorizing agricultural waste and promoting sustainable resource utilization.

papers.title: CRDS-Unet: channel-reversed depthwise separable U-net for efficient tomato leaf disease segmentation
papers.journal: Frontiers in Food Science and Technology
papers.abstract: Introduction Automated plant leaf disease segmentation is crucial for accurate disease diagnosis and quantitative lesion assessment in precision agriculture. U-Net-based architectures are widely employed for this task, although their high computational complexity sometimes hinders their application in resource-constrained agricultural settings. Methods This work investigates depthwise separable convolutions in conjunction with a channel-reversed U-Net for tomato leaf disease segmentation. The channel-reversed encoder allocates more feature channels to the shallow layers and progressively fewer to the deeper layers, the reverse of a conventional U-Net’s channel schedule, with the aim of preserving spatial detail while reducing computation in the deeper, more computationally expensive stages. Depthwise separable convolutions are used throughout the encoder, bottleneck, and decoder to further reduce trainable parameters. The model was trained on lesion masks and evaluated on an independent, held-out subset of the PlantVillage tomato leaf dataset using Dice coefficient, IoU, precision, recall, and F1-score, following a corrected data-splitting protocol that eliminates train/test leakage present in an earlier version of this work. Results The proposed method reduced trainable parameters by over 97% relative to a conventional U-Net (0.96 million versus 31.06 million), at a measured reduction in segmentation accuracy under the training budget evaluated (Dice coefficient 0.79 versus 0.90 for standard U-Net). A supplementary experiment with a longer training budget narrowed this gap substantially (Dice coefficient 0.85). Discussion These findings indicate that the parameter-efficient design requires more training to approach the accuracy of higher-parameter alternatives. We report this accuracy/efficiency trade-off directly, rather than claiming accuracy parity, and identify a full matched-budget comparison across all evaluated architectures as a priority for follow-up work. By demonstrating a substantial, disclosed parameter-efficiency gain, this approach is intended to support future development of low-cost disease diagnosis tools for resource-constrained agricultural settings. Validated real-time, on-device deployment remains a direction for future work.

Results The proposed method reduced trainable parameters by over 97% relative to a conventional U-Net (0.96 million versus 31.06 million), at a measured reduction in segmentation accuracy under the training budget evaluated (Dice coefficient 0.79 versus 0.90 for standard U-Net). papers.title: Development of a machine learning-based treatment-response prediction model for levetiracetam in pediatric epilepsy: integrating ABCB1 polymorphism and therapeutic drug monitoring
papers.abstract: Background Empirical dosing of levetiracetam (LEV) in pediatric epilepsy often yields variable outcomes. This study aimed to develop a machine learning-based treatment-response prediction model integrating therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) and ABCB1 C3435 T polymorphism. Methods Clinical, TDM, and genetic data from 346 pediatric patients were retrospectively analyzed. Four machine learning algorithms were evaluated. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was utilized to interpret feature associations. Results The XGBoost model demonstrated the highest predictive performance (AUC=0.893). SHAP analysis indicated that LEV trough concentration (C min ) and ABCB1 genotype were the strongest associative factors for clinical outcomes. The homozygous TT mutation was associated with treatment resistance despite adequate peripheral C min . SHAP interaction patterns generated an exploratory hypothesis that ABCB1 genotype may modify the associative relationship between systemic exposure and treatment response. Conclusion Integrating ABCB1 genotyping and TDM via the XGBoost model may provides an interpretable approach for predicting LEV treatment response in pediatric epilepsy. Rather than directly generating individualized dosing regimens, these associative findings offer a hypothesis-generating reference for identifying patients at risk of therapeutic failure, warranting further prospective exposure-response validation.

papers.title: How do virtual streamers turn viewership traffic into sales? Consumer behavior mechanisms from an interaction characteristics perspective
papers.abstract: 摘要： 人工智能驱动的虚拟主播能够作为真人主播的补充, 在直播带货中与消费者互动, 然而直播效果参差不齐, 这影响了其在电商直播领域的广泛应用。本研究从虚拟主播交互特征的视角研究消费者购买决策行为的影响因素及其作用机制。具体包括: (1)虚拟主播形象对消费者购前行为的影响, 以及产品信息呈现的调节作用; (2)虚拟主播沟通风格对消费者购前行为的影响, 以及消费者特征和产品类型的调节作用; (3)消费者对虚拟主播服务质量的购后口碑评价。本研究构建了信息与情感双路径整合分析框架, 弥补了现有研究对虚拟主播交互机制与购后行为影响机制缺乏探讨的不足, 拓展了电商直播与消费者在线行为领域的理论边界。在实践层面, 该框架为提升消费者直播参与度、优化购买决策, 以及推动数字经济与电子商务高质量发展提供了理论支撑。

papers.title: Bilateral asymmetric dependence and partner country trade network resilience: empirical evidence from China’s rare earth trade
papers.abstract: Background Against the backdrop of intensifying competition for critical mineral security, rare earth trade has become a crucial window for observing supply chain restructuring and great power rivalry. Methods Drawing on the 2013–2024 UN Comtrade data on rare earth full-industry-chain trade, this article measures the structural trade network resilience of China’s rare earth trading partners at the partner country level, and examines the impact of China’s bilateral asymmetric dependence on its trading partners on their trade network resilience within a two-way fixed effects framework. Results The results show that upstream export dependence asymmetry is significantly negatively associated with partner country resilience, and that this negative association operates mainly through the structural stability and diversification dimensions, remaining robust under endogeneity treatments such as system GMM. The moderating-effect and heterogeneity analyses indicate that the negative association is more pronounced among partner countries with stronger resource endowments and weaker manufacturing bases, and that partner countries with lower income levels and higher trade openness are likewise more vulnerable. Further analysis shows that midstream and downstream import dependence is not significantly associated with resilience, and that no significant reverse association is found. Discussion This article contributes to understanding the consequences of dependence in strategic mineral trade and its boundary conditions from the partner country perspective.

papers.title: Predictive modelling of conducting Casson nanofluid flow using a physics-informed neural network: effects of thermal stratification and coupled transport mechanisms
papers.journal: Frontiers in Applied Mathematics and Statistics
papers.abstract: Conducting Casson nanofluid flow with thermal stratification plays vital role in advanced heat and mass transfer processes such as energy conversion, polymer processing, metallurgical operations, and biomedical applications. The simultaneous influence of magnetic fields, porous-medium resistance, Joule and Darcy dissipation, thermal radiation, Brownian motion, thermophoresis, and chemical reactions creates a strongly coupled nonlinear boundary-value problem that is difficult to solve using conventional analytical or numerical methods. To address this challenge, present study examines flow, heat-transfer, and mass-transfer behaviour of conducting Casson nanofluid over exponentially expanding permeable surface, incorporating thermal stratification along with aforementioned physical effects. Governing equations are reduced to a system of nonlinear ordinary differential equations through similarity transformations. Physics-Informed Neural Network framework is developed to obtain predictive solutions by embedding the governing equations, boundary conditions and loss function. PINN utilizes automatic differentiation and a two-stage training strategy with Adam and L-BFGS optimizers. The numerical performance of the PINN is assessed using governing-equation residual metrics, including MSE, MAE, and RMSE. The MSE ranges from 4.74 × 10 −7 to 5.55 × 10 −3 , the MAE from 4.75 × 10 −4 to 5.32 × 10 −2 , and the RMSE from 6.89 × 10 −4 to 7.45 × 10 −2 across the reported parameter cases. These metrics quantify residual satisfaction of the governing equations rather than errors relative to an external reference solution. Agreement with an independently computed boundary-value solution is assessed separately through comparisons of the solution profiles and wall quantities for selected parameter cases. Overall, the results demonstrate the applicability of the PINN framework to the coupled nonlinear conducting Casson nanofluid problem. Independent comparison with a boundary-value solution was conducted for the baseline case and the parameter variations R d = 1.5 and S c = 0.6. The agreement in the wall quantities for these selected cases supports the numerical consistency of the PINN predictions under the conditions examined. These findings are limited to the evaluated cases and do not establish convergence or low solution error across the entire parameter range.
papers.summary: Conducting Casson nanofluid flow with thermal stratification plays vital role in advanced heat and mass transfer processes such as energy conversion, polymer processing, metallurgical operations, and biomedical applications. The numerical performance of the PINN is assessed using governing-equation residual metrics, including MSE, MAE, and RMSE. Overall, the results demonstrate the applicability of the PINN framework to the coupled nonlinear conducting Casson nanofluid problem.

papers.title: Matériaux composites céramiques recyclés intégrant un MCP pour la récupération de chaleur fatale industrielle
papers.abstract: En France, l’industrie représentait environ 18,4 % de la consommation nationale d’énergie finale en 2023 avec une forte dépendance aux combustibles fossiles et à l’électricité pour la production de chaleur alors qu’à l’échelle de l’Union Européenne, plus de 50% de la demande totale des industries métallurgique, chimique et céramique nécessite une production de chaleur à plus de 500°C. L’objectif de ces travaux est de développer un composite céramique - matériaux à changement de phase (MCP) destiné au stockage thermique haute température (500-800 °C). Ces composites sont des structures architecturées poreuses, imprimées en 3D à partir de matières premières recyclées, élaborées (IRCER) imprégnées de MCP inorganiques ou métalliques (LaTEP et LaSIE). Un composite eutectique Al-Si (88-12 % massique, température de fusion de 577 °C) - mélange céramique (andalousite, fumée de silice, SiC, ciment d’aluminates de calcium fourni par IMERYS) a été retenu (50 % massique chacun). Des échantillons sous forme de pastilles ont été formés par pressage uniaxial (100 MPa) puis ont subi un traitement thermique à 600 °C (air) pour oxyder l’AlSi et consolider la matrice. Les matériaux ont été caractérisés par MEB, Raman (détection de alpha-Al2O3) et DSC (40-600 °C, air et Ar). La microstructure révèle une matrice poreuse et une cohésion limitée, liées à une hydratation insuffisante du ciment. Les particules d’AlSi sont encapsulées dans une coquille d’alpha-alumine, assurant le confinement du MCP. Les mesures DSC montrent une fusion à 576-582 °C et une chaleur latente de 218 J/g, stable sur plusieurs cycles et sans fuite. Ces résultats sont prometteurs. En effet, La structure entièrement solide et la compatibilité chimique Al2O3/matrice facilitent l’intégration future en impression 3D et l’ajout de MCP complémentaires tout en assurant une stabilité chimique et thermique des matériaux

papers.title: Mechanism of Polyacrylonitrile-Based Carbon Fiber Carbonization Optimization by Fullerene for High-Performance Carbon Fibers
papers.abstract: Abstract Enhancement arising for polyacrylonitrile (PAN)-based carbon fibers from C60 fullerene, which possesses a unique zero-dimensional structure and similar nano-scale dimensions, remains rarely reported and merits investigation. In this study, C60@PAN precursor fibers were fabricated via wet spinning and subsequently subjected to stabilization and carbonization, yielding composite carbon fibers with superior properties that were compared against neat PAN-based carbon fibers by means of X-ray diffraction (XRD), Raman spectroscopy, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and other characterization techniques. Through multi-scale structural characterization, combined with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and first-principles density functional theory (DFT) calculations, mechanisms underlying C60-induced reinforcement in PAN-based carbon fibers were systematically explored. Experimental and characterization results revealed that incorporation of C60 did not impair spinnability of PAN; composite precursor fibers exhibited a uniform and continuous morphology without significant defects. During stabilization, C60 reduced activation energy of cyclization reactions, moderated exothermic behavior, and provided structural support via an induced crystallization effect. After carbonization, composite fibers exhibit a markedly improved carbon layer stacking order, graphitization degree, and a concurrent increase in char yield. MD and DFT further disclosed that C60 dispersed homogeneously in PAN at room temperature, facilitating uniform orientation of PAN chains; at elevated temperatures, gradual fragmentation and fusion of conjugated cage structures of C60 served as critical templates for enhancing carbon structural ordering. This study elucidates the promoting mechanism of C60 in a favorable microstructural arrangement of PAN precursor fibers and subsequent stabilization−carbonization processes, offering experimental evidence and theoretical guidance for structural optimization and performance enhancement of high-performance PAN-based carbon fibers. The high-performance carbon fibers fabricated via this strategy find applications in commercial aerospace and low-altitude aircraft sectors. Moreover, the variations in electrical properties induced by C60 incorporation also warrant further investigation in the fields of capacitors and batteries.

papers.title: Silica–Lignin Composites—Insight into Physicochemical Properties and Adsorption Mechanisms
papers.abstract: Two silica–lignin composites with varying biopolymer content were synthesized using the sol–gel method as effective adsorbents for the removal of organic dyes from aqueous solutions. The textural, structural, and surface properties of the synthesized materials were determined using nitrogen adsorption–desorption techniques, XRD, XPS, and FTIR. XPS and XRD analysis confirmed the effective modification of the silica surface with lignin. Increasing the lignin content in the composite altered its physicochemical properties. Textural analysis revealed a decrease in the porosity of the composites with increasing the amount of biopolymer incorporated into the silica. Thermal analysis with the identification of gaseous thermal destruction products allowed for the determination of the thermal stability of the composites. Dye adsorption experiments, including equilibrium and kinetic measurements, allowed the determination of adsorption capacity, adsorption rate and adsorption mechanisms. FTIR mapping enabled the identification of differences in the interactions of selected dyes with the synthesized composites and revealed preferential adsorption on surface areas of the adsorbents rich in lignin or silica. The obtained results confirmed the potential of silica–lignin materials in environmental applications as cheap and biodegradable adsorbents.

papers.title: FORMULATION, OPTIMIZATION AND EVALUATION OF ANTIBACTERIAL NANOPARTICLE-LOADED IN SITU GEL FOR ENHANCED OCULAR DRUG DELIVERY
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Bacterial conjunctivitis is a common ocular infection requiring effective antimicrobial therapy. Conventional ophthalmic preparations of ciprofloxacin hydrochloride have limited ocular residence time due to tear drainage and blinking, which may reduce therapeutic effectiveness. The present study aimed to formulate, optimize and evaluate ciprofloxacin hydrochloride-loaded chitosan nanoparticles incorporated into a thermoreversible in situ gel for enhanced ocular drug delivery. Ciprofloxacin hydrochloride was characterized by preformulation studies, showing a λmax of 277 nm, saturation solubility of 13.6 ± 0.05 mg/mL in distilled water and 11.4 ± 0.05 mg/mL in simulated tear fluid, an average melting point of 316°C and a DSC endothermic peak at 319°C. FTIR studies confirmed drug identity and compatibility with the selected excipients. Nanoparticles were prepared by ionic gelation using chitosan and sodium tripolyphosphate and optimized using a central composite design. The optimized nanoparticles containing 0.2% chitosan and 0.1% tripolyphosphate exhibited a particle size of 266.8 nm, PDI of 0.25, zeta potential of +20.6 mV, entrapment efficiency of 71.05% and drug content of 35.5%. SEM confirmed spherical nanoparticles. The optimized nanoparticles were incorporated into 19% w/v Poloxamer 407 in situ gel. The formulation showed a gelation temperature of 35.36 ± 0.31°C, gelation time of 66 seconds, pH of 7.2 ± 0.2, solution viscosity of 130 ± 4.1 and gel viscosity of 6454 ± 4.5, with 83% drug content. In vitro release reached 78.5% at 8 hours and followed the Korsmeyer–Peppas model (R² = 0.9954; n = 1.4886), indicating Super Case-II transport. Ex vivo corneal permeation reached 41.07% at 4 hours. The formulation showed antibacterial activity against S. aureus and E. coli, with zones of inhibition of 3.1 ± 0.2 and 3.4 ± 1.2 cm, respectively. Thus, the developed formulation demonstrated sustained drug release, corneal permeation and promising antibacterial activity, indicating its potential for ocular delivery of ciprofloxacin hydrochloride.
papers.summary: Bacterial conjunctivitis is a common ocular infection requiring effective antimicrobial therapy. The present study aimed to formulate, optimize and evaluate ciprofloxacin hydrochloride-loaded chitosan nanoparticles incorporated into a thermoreversible in situ gel for enhanced ocular drug delivery. Thus, the developed formulation demonstrated sustained drug release, corneal permeation and promising antibacterial activity, indicating its potential for ocular delivery of ciprofloxacin hydrochloride.

papers.title: Valorization of Cashew Industry Waste into Anacardate-Based Green Foaming Agents for Foam Concrete Applications
papers.journal: Journal of Materials in Civil Engineering
papers.abstract: Abstract Traditional foaming agents and foam concrete rely on synthetic chemicals and ordinary portland cement (OPC) with a high carbon footprint. This paper presents the formulation of novel anacardate-based green foaming agents derived from cashew industry waste to address the environmental concerns associated with synthetic surfactants. Unsaturated and saturated anacardic acids were extracted and modified using sodium and potassium-based alkalis to synthesize anionic surfactants. The salts of unsaturated anacardic acid-ene mixture demonstrated superior foaming capabilities over their saturated counterparts, which exhibited unfavorable gelling behavior in an aqueous solution. This is beneficial considering the economy and sustainability; as an intermediate, extracting unsaturated anacardic acid is straightforward, less energy-intensive, and more cost-efficient than extracting saturated anacardic acid. Disodium anacardate (unsaturated) yielded foam with favorable density and stability but required further stabilization for use in foam concrete. Thus, three polymer admixtures, namely, xanthan gum, guar gum, and sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (Na-CMC), were investigated. Xanthan gum showed maximum viscosity enhancement of foaming solution and foam stabilization, followed by Na-CMC and guar gum. The compatibility of the stabilized disodium anacardate (unsaturated) foaming agents with both OPC and geopolymer binders was evaluated in terms of reaction kinetics, fresh-state stability, compressive strength, and water absorption. Isothermal calorimetry results confirmed that the anacardate-based foaming agent did not retard binder reactions, irrespective of the admixture used. Further, geopolymer foam concrete exhibited higher compressive strength and lower water absorption than OPC-based mixes at comparable densities, indicating a better synergy. Thus, anacardate-based foams offer a viable, sustainable alternative to synthetic surfactants in foam concrete.

papers.title: Lunar Organic Output Neutralization and Advanced Recovery (LOO-NAR): A conceptual framework and feasibility review for human waste pyrolysis
papers.abstract: Long-duration lunar habitation will require technologies that convert crew-generated wastes into recoverable resources while operating within strict limits on mass, power, volume, reliability, and resupply. Human fecal waste and associated sanitation materials remain a major unresolved stream because current spacecraft systems emphasize collection and containment rather than downstream conversion. This review assesses the potential applicability of pyrolysis to lunar human-waste management by synthesizing evidence from human feces, simulated fecal material, fecal sludge, biosolids, sanitation-related materials, and relevant terrestrial analogs. The analysis examines torrefaction, intermediate-temperature pyrolysis, and high-temperature conversion with emphasis on product yields, gas composition, biochar properties, aqueous pyrolysis liquid treatment, contaminant fate, reactor design, and habitat integration. Across the literature, pyrolysis shows potential to support waste stabilization, moisture recovery, solid-waste reduction, biochar production, and non-condensable gas generation, but performance varies with feedstock composition and operating conditions. Based on this evidence, the review introduces Lunar Organic Output Neutralization and Advanced Recovery, or LOO-NAR, as a mission-adaptive conceptual framework linking sealed collection, pre-drying, staged thermal conversion, product separation, gas cleanup, heat recovery, water treatment, and selective resource use. The framework is designed to allow treatment intensity and product recovery to increase as mission duration and resource demands increase. Human fecal waste and sanitation materials form the baseline feedstock, with future potential for compatible organic outputs. Key gaps include reduced-gravity and vacuum validation, mixed-feedstock variability, contaminant control, product quality, long-duration reliability, and integrated systems and equivalent system mass evaluation. These findings identify a focused validation pathway for assessing the potential future lunar application of LOO-NAR.

papers.title: Reactive Decaborane Initiates Low-Temperature Polymer Decomposition and Drives Ceramic Formation
papers.abstract: Abstract Boron carbide (B4C) is a ceramic of considerable interest due to its high hardness, elevated melting point, excellent thermal stability, low density, and chemical inertness. Decaborane-functionalized preceramic polymers (PCPs) prepared from ring-opening metathesis polymerization (ROMP) are excellent single-source precursors of B4C, but the mechanistic details for the decomposition and ceramic conversion during pyrolysis have been overlooked, preventing advances in redesigning preceramic polymers that have high char yields and desirable chemical compositions. Herein, we reveal insights into the role of decaborane during the polymer-to-ceramic transition of poly(cyclooctenyldecaborane) (PCD) to boron carbide. ROMP of the cyclooctenyldecaborane monomer enabled controllable molecular weight and produced a series of polymers with molecular weights up to 35 kg/mol and dispersities (D̵) in the range of 1.3-1.6. Thermogravimetric analysis coupled with infrared spectroscopy and mass spectrometry (TGA-IR and TGA-MS, respectively) of PCD revealed the evolution of small hydrocarbon species following an initial release of hydrogen at low decomposition temperatures around 250 °C, which is in stark contrast to the decomposition profile of unfunctionalized poly(cyclooctadiene) (PCOD) that transitions into volatile hydrocarbon species at approximately 450 °C. ReaxFF molecular dynamics (MD) simulations support the experimental findings that hydrogen release from decaborane initiates the polymer-to-ceramic conversion. MD simulations indicate that the release of H2 results in the exothermic formation of boron clusters, which promote the thermal decomposition of the hydrocarbon polymer backbone. These findings indicate that decaborane plays an active role in the polymer-to-ceramic conversion rather than serving solely as a boron source, providing mechanistic insight that will enable the rational design of next-generation PCPs with enhanced ceramic yields and tunable compositions.

papers.title: Hawthorn Polysaccharide Alleviates Cyclophosphamide-Induced Immunosuppression and Intestinal Mucosal Injury in Mice
papers.abstract: Immunosuppression and intestinal mucosal injury are relevant concerns in animal health.Plant-derived polysaccharides have attracted interest as potential immunomodulators, although evidence from experimental models requires further evaluation before veterinary application.This study evaluated the effects of hawthorn polysaccharide (HP) on cyclophosphamide (Cy)-induced immunosuppression and intestinal mucosal injury in mice.The results showed that HP alleviated Cy-induced systemic immunosuppression and intestinal mucosal injury, as reflected by improvements in immune organ indices, hematological parameters, mucosal morphology, goblet cell abundance, inflammatory and mucosal immune parameters, and barrier-related proteins.High-dose HP was also associated with changes in Cyrelated intestinal transcriptional profiles, particularly those involving cell-cycle-and proliferation-related processes, together with alterations in gut microbial composition.The associations among bacterial taxa, representative genes, and barrier indicators suggest that these responses occurred in parallel during HP intervention.Although the underlying causal relationships require further verification, the findings support further study of HP as a potential immunomodulator, with its relevance to veterinary use requiring evaluation in the intended animal species.

papers.title: DIAGNOSTIC ACCURACY OF ULTRA-LOW-DOSE CT VS. STANDARD-DOSE CT FOR PULMONARY NODULE DETECTION: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND META-ANALYSIS
authors: KHALED BONNA , RASHA GALAL ELSAFTY , NORA EID ALANAZI , RANIN JABER M ALMAJRASHI AHLAM ALI Y ASIRI , WALEED MUFAREH ALSHAHRANI , SOMAYYAH SOHAIL MITHA , SHOUG NASSER ALKHAMMASH , BANDAR SAAD ALSHREEF
papers.journal: TPM Testing, psychometrics, methodology in applied psychology
papers.abstract: Background: Standard dose computed tomography (CT) is a primary modality for detecting pulmonary nodules (PNs), but the health risk from cumulative radiation exposure has prompted the emergence of ultra-low-dose CT (ULDCT) as an alternative to reduce this dose, because its diagnostic accuracy remains variable, this systematic review and meta-analysis aims to synthesize the existing evidence to determine the diagnostic accuracy and effective radiation dose of ULDCT for pulmonary nodule detection. Methods: Following PRISMA guidelines, a systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Cochrane Library, and Ovid MEDLINE for original research published between 2015 and 2025 that evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of ULDCT for PN detection, for which a meta-analysis using random-effects models was performed to calculate the pooled sensitivity for nodule detection and the pooled mean effective radiation dose, with a subgroup analysis conducted to assess the impact of different reconstruction algorithms. Results: Forty-two studies comprising 15,792 patients were included, from which a meta-analysis of 11 studies demonstrated a pooled sensitivity of 91.9% (95% CI: 84.6%–97.1%) for PN detection with heterogeneity (I²=93.0%), and a pooled mean effective dose from 12 studies of 0.22 mSv (95% CI: 0.11–0.33 mSv), a level comparable to standard chest radiography, while subgroup analysis revealed a trend towards higher sensitivity with advanced reconstruction algorithms (96.7%) compared to standard iterative reconstruction (87.9%) that was not statistically significant (p=0.091), and a narrative synthesis confirmed ULDCT's accuracy for solid nodules but identified reduced sensitivity for subsolid, ground-glass, and small (<6 mm) nodules, with performance limited in patients with a high body mass index (BMI). Conclusion: ULDCT combined with advanced reconstruction techniques offers high diagnostic accuracy for the detection of solid pulmonary nodules and reduces radiation exposure to levels approaching that of a chest X-ray, but its utility is limited for detecting subsolid and small nodules and in obese patients, making protocol standardization and patient-specific considerations essential to optimize its clinical implementation.

papers.title: Impacts of Polymeric Excipients on the Physicochemical Properties of Ritonavir Solid Dispersions
papers.journal: VNU Journal of Science Medical and Pharmaceutical Sciences
papers.abstract: Abstract: Amorphous solid dispersion (ASD) formulation prepared by solvent‑evaporation was employed to enhance the apparent solubility of the poorly water‑soluble drug ritonavir (RTV), a BCS Class IV compound widely used in HIV therapy. This study investigated the influence of polymeric excipients on ritonavir’s solid‑state form, apparent solubility, and dissolution behavior in ASDs prepared by the film casting–solvent evaporation. Thermal analysis and X‑ray diffraction examination (DSC, XRD) demonstrated a complete conversion of RTV from the crystalline to the amorphous state in most formulations, except the formulation containing 50% Copovidone, where total amorphization was not achieved. FTIR spectroscopy indicated non‑covalent interactions between RTV and polymers such as hydroxypropyl methylcellulose acetyl succinate (HPMCAS) and hydroxypropyl methylcellulose phtalate (HPMCP). Among the screened polymers, HPMCAS and Copovidone promoted the greatest improvement in apparent solubility, up to approximately 22-to-30-fold relative to crystalline RTV. Dissolution testing results exhibited that formulations containing HPMC P55, Eudragit L100‑55 and Eudragit E100 provided superior drug release. Increasing drug load in the ASD inversely influenced both the enhancement of apparent solubility and the ability to sustain supersaturation; high drug fractions in the solid dispersion promoted phase separation and surface precipitation of RTV, which impeded diffusion and reduced dissolution performance. Intrinsic dissolution and diffusion assays underscore the critical role of polymer selection in modulating molecular mobility and stabilizing the amorphous drug. Overall, findings in this study provide a scientific basis for applying amorphous solid dispersion to improve dissolution and enhance apparent solubility of ritonavir through appropriate polymer selection and drug loading optimization. Keywords: Amorphous solid dispersion (ASD), Ritonavir, Apparent solubility, Intrinsic dissolution rate.

papers.title: Synergistic Absorption Mechanism in Flexible Polymer Composites Reinforced with Rare Earth Cobaltite and Molybdenum Carbide for EMI Shielding Applications
papers.abstract: Abstract The sudden growth of digital devices and fifth-generation (5G) communication systems has generated increasing concerns regarding electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding in advanced technological applications, due to the high necessity for development of flexible, lightweight and efficient shielding materials. In this study, low thickness polymer composite films based on poly(vinylidene fluoride) polymer that is incorporated with gadolinium cobaltite and molybdenum carbide fillers were successfully fabricated through a solution casting technique. The chemical, structural, and morphological characteristics of the composite films were investigated using XRD, FTIR, FESEM, HR-TEM, tensile strength and contact angle. Thermal stability was assessed through thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), and electromagnetic properties were evaluated in terms of complex permittivity and permeability across the X-band frequency range. The EMI shielding was examined in terms of shielding effectiveness due to absorption, reflection, and transmission and further validated using CST software. The selected composite film with an ultralow thickness of ∼0.15 mm exhibited a maximum EMI shielding efficiency of ∼49 dB in the X-band region with the absorption dominant shielding as the primary attenuation mechanism. The composite films displayed an enhanced mechanical strength and hydrophobicity behavior, making them suitable for flexible and durable shielding applications. These results suggest that the developed PVDF/GdCoO3/Mo2C composite films are promising candidates for advanced electromagnetic interference shielding applications in wearable electronics, stealth technology, and defense systems.

These results suggest that the developed PVDF/GdCoO3/Mo2C composite films are promising candidates for advanced electromagnetic interference shielding applications in wearable electronics, stealth technology, and defense systems.

papers.title: Deep Learning for AD Risk Screening and Progression Prediction
papers.abstract: Timely intervention for Alzheimer's disease (AD) requires early detection. The development of immunotherapies targeting amyloid-beta and tau underscores the need for accessible, time-efficient biomarkers for early diagnosis. Here, we directly applied our previously developed MRI-based deep learning model for AD to the large Chinese SILCODE cohort (722 participants, 1,105 brain MRI scans). The model - initially trained on North American data - demonstrated robust cross-ethnic generalization, without any retraining or fine-tuning, achieving an AUC of 91.3% in AD classification with a sensitivity of 95.2%. It successfully identified 86.7% of individuals at risk of AD progression more than 5 years in advance. Individuals identified as high-risk exhibited significantly shorter median progression times. By integrating an interpretable deep learning brain risk map approach, we identified AD brain subtypes, including an MCI subtype associated with rapid cognitive decline. The model's risk scores showed significant correlations with cognitive measures and plasma biomarkers, such as tau proteins and neurofilament light chain (NfL). These findings underscore the exceptional generalizability and clinical utility of MRI-based deep learning models, especially in large and diverse populations, offering valuable tools for early therapeutic intervention. The model has been made open-source and deployed to a free online website for AD risk prediction, to assist in early screening and intervention.

papers.title: Structure–Performance Relationships in Metal–Organic Framework Mg 2 (olz) Catalysts for CO 2 Adsorption and Hydrogenation to Methanol
papers.abstract: We investigated a Cu–Zn‐modified Mg 2 (olz) catalyst for carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) hydrogenation to methanol under low CO 2 partial pressures, relevant to dilute CO 2 streams in industrial gas treatment and carbon capture. The catalyst was prepared via wet impregnation of presynthesized Cu–Zn species into the metal‐organic framework (MOF). Batch tests under mild temperatures and low CO 2 concentration showed that the MOF‐based system achieved higher methanol yields than a commercial catalyst at 150 °C. Step‐response experiments in a plug‐flow reactor revealed that the MOF retained a significant amount of CO 2 under high‐pressure and dynamic conditions. In situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy identified methanol‐related surface intermediates, while ex situ postreaction 1 H nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy supported the formation and retention of methanol and oxygenated species in the MOF‐based catalyst. X‐ray absorption spectroscopy showed partial reduction of oxygenated Cu species during reaction, while in situ X‐ray diffraction demonstrated structural stability of the Mg 2 (olz) MOF framework. These results indicate that Mg 2 (olz)‐based materials combine CO 2 adsorption capacity with catalytic functionality. Adsorption and catalytic functions coexist rather than being directly coupled. The material exhibits methanol productivity at low temperature in the presence of a solvent phase and remains structurally stable under the investigated catalytic conditions.

papers.title: MadAgents
papers.abstract: We uncover an effective and communicative set of agents working with MadGraph. Agentic installation, learning-by-doing training, and user support provide easy access to state-of-the-art simulations and accelerate LHC research. We show in detail how MadAgents interact with inexperienced and advanced users, support a range of simulation tasks, and analyze the results. In a second step, we illustrate how MadAgents automatize event generation and run an autonomous simulation campaign, starting from a pdf file of a paper. We also present successive MadAgents updates, including a Claude Code implementation with a self-improvement loop.

papers.title: Stromal VEGF-C expression predicts nodal metastasis: implications for axillary surgery de-escalation in breast cancer
papers.abstract: Abstract Accurate preoperative prediction of lymph node metastasis (LNM) is critical for de-escalating breast cancer surgery, sparing node-negative patients the morbidity of sentinel lymph node biopsy while ensuring appropriate staging for those at risk. Yet reliable molecular predictors of LNM remain lacking. VEGF-C, a key driver of lymphangiogenesis, is expressed in both cancer cell and stromal compartments, but its clinical utility is unclear. In a prospectively enrolled cohort, we assessed stromal and cancer cell VEGF-C expression by immunohistochemistry using both manual scoring and a novel automated image analysis script enabling objective, reproducible quantification of stromal versus epithelial VEGF-C fractions at scale. Stromal VEGF-C was independently associated with LNM after adjustment for established predictors (P = 0.004), with prediction models reaching AUCs of up to 0.784. Cancer cell VEGF-C added no predictive value. Critically, stromal VEGF-C showed potential to replace vascular invasion, which is a strong but preoperatively inaccessible predictor in LNM prediction models. Stromal VEGF-C assessment in preoperative biopsies could therefore enable more precise nodal staging, supporting informed surgical decision-making and the identification of patients who may safely avoid unnecessary axillary intervention.

papers.title: The two-level systems in cryogenic solids, or how to avoid stressful memories
papers.abstract: Structural glasses prepared by bulk quenching a liquid melt universally exhibit puzzling low-energy excitations commonly known as the ‘two-level systems’ (TLSs). Recent studies indicate that ultrastable glassy films made by vapor deposition exhibit substantially fewer TLSs and, at the same time, are more stable enthalpically than conventional glasses made by quenching a melt. A similar phenomenon is observed in very stable glasses of model liquid mixtures prepared using swap Monte Carlo sampling. However, in a separate set of enthalpically stable solids, exemplified by amber matured over geological times, the two-level systems persist. In addressing this seeming conflict, we emphasize that a depletion of the TLSs, if any, means the configurational entropy of the material is lower than that of conventional glasses made by bulk-quenching a melt. Ageing does induce reduction in configurational entropy, but amber, we speculate, achieves enthalpic stabilization through increased bonding, not ageing. We separately comment on the discrepancy among existing predictions for the extent of cooperativity of the two-level systems. Several experiments are suggested to test the present picture.

A similar phenomenon is observed in very stable glasses of model liquid mixtures prepared using swap Monte Carlo sampling. Several experiments are suggested to test the present picture.

papers.title: CERES: a cryogenic experiment to reconstruct energy systematics in $$\hbox {TeO}_2$$ bolometers
papers.abstract: Abstract Cryogenic calorimetric detectors are a powerful tool in the search for rare events such as neutrinoless double beta decay ( $$0\nu \beta \beta $$ 0 ν β β ), due to their excellent energy resolution and low intrinsic background. The performance of these detectors depends critically on a precise understanding of their energy scale and energy resolution. Recent studies suggest that both energy scale and energy resolution may vary depending on the spatial location and topology of energy deposition within the detector, indicating the presence of previously uncharacterized systematic effects. The Cryogenic Experiment to Reconstruct Energy Systematics (CERES) is a dedicated experiment designed to directly measure the position dependence of calorimetric response in Tellurium Dioxide ( $$\hbox {TeO}_{2}$$ TeO 2 ) crystals. This paper details the experimental design, current status, and future upgrade plans for CERES.

papers.title: GaN Nucleation Landscape on Patterned Sapphire Shaped by the Growth Temperature of Directly Grown Boron-Compound Masks
papers.abstract: Abstract The growth temperature of directly grown boron-compound masks on patterned sapphire is associated with changes in the inferred effective accessibility of the underlying sapphire surface and in the subsequent nucleation behavior of GaN. In this work, we investigate how ammonia-borane-derived boron-compound masks grown at different temperatures shape the GaN nucleation landscape within circular SiO2 openings during the initial stage of epitaxial lateral overgrowth. The preferential nucleation position of GaN changes systematically with mask growth temperature: masks grown at 700−750 °C produce pronounced edge-biased distributions, whereas higher-temperature masks lead to more inward-shifted and spatially sparse GaN domains. Quantitative analysis of the GaN areal fraction, the number of visibly isolated domains, and the radial distribution of domain centers show that the mask growth temperature affects both the amount of GaN coverage and the spatial arrangement of GaN domains within each opening. The nonmonotonic change in the number of visibly isolated domains is interpreted as a consequence of competition between reduced lateral merging and reduced effective substrate accessibility rather than as a direct measure of the number of active nucleation sites. Coarse-grained kMC-type simulations provide a qualitative consistency test by varying the effective density and radial distribution of substrate-accessible sites. These results suggest that the growth temperature of directly formed boron-compound masks can serve as a pre-growth process parameter for tuning the early-stage intra-opening GaN nucleation landscape. This behavior is described in terms of effective substrate accessibility inferred from the GaN nucleation morphology, while the microscopic origin of the accessible regions remains to be resolved by direct structural characterization.

papers.title: Synthesis and characterization of 2-methylimidazole end capped Zwitter ion functionalized Polyaniline
papers.abstract: Abstract Due to the lack of functional groups, the processability of polyanilines (PANIs) are limited. Poor solubility in common solvents, high rigidity and hydrophobicity are the important problems associated with PANI. To enhance its processability, acid and amine groups were grafted onto the PANI backbone via a Friedel-Crafts (FC) alkylation reaction, carried out at 85°C for 6 hours under a nitrogen atmosphere with vigorous stirring. Prior to this, the PANI backbone was synthesized through free radical (FR) solution polymerization, initiated by peroxy disulphate (PDS), using aniline monomer at 0–5°C under nitrogen purging. A key modification during synthesis was the inclusion of 2 -methylimidazole ( 2 MI), which imparted hydrophilicity and facilitated end-capping of the polymer chains. The functionalized PANIs were thoroughly characterized by various analytical tools, antimicrobial properties and thermal properties. Following acid functionalization, the water contact angle (WCA) increased to 61.4°, attributed to the formation of Zwitter ionic structures, as evidenced by an FTIR peak at 1640 cm⁻¹. This modification also significantly improved the water solubility of PANI. The % yield of A3 sample was found to be low due to the availability of few reaction cite on the aromatic ring of PANI for second grafting reaction. A plausible reaction mechanism was proposed based on the experimental findings, which were carefully analyzed and compared with values reported in the literature.

papers.title: Characterization of the organelle genomes of mycoheterotrophic Thismia angustimitra and evidence suggesting horizontal gene transfer
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Our knowledge about mitochondrial genome evolution in plants is lacking far behind our knowledge of plastome evolution. In heterotrophic plants, it is well-known that plastome degradation and reduced or lost photosynthesis go hand in hand, and there is little if any difference between plastome evolution in mycoheterotrophic and haustorial parasites. The mitochondrial genome appears less affected by a heterotrophic lifestyle, although exceptions occur. In contrast to plastome evolution, mitochondrial evolution may differ between mycoheterotrophic and haustorial parasites, in particular with regards to the occurrence of horizontal gene transfer. However, data from mycoheterotrophs are scarce, and complete mitogenomes are only known from three of ten clades. Results Here we present data from the complete plastome and mitogenome from Thismia angustimitra , representing a fourth clade of mycoheterotrophs. The 18,215 bp plastome is much reduced and includes only few genes. The mitogenome has a multicircular structure consisting of 22 chromosomes with a total length of 422,400 bp. The gene content and the pattern of RNA editing are normal. The mitogenome includes only few repeats and recombinational activity is limited. A search for foreign DNA did not reveal any fungal sequences, and the content of plastid DNA is low. Just a few inserts appear to have originated through intracellular transfer, whereas others most likely stem from horizontal gene transfer. Conclusion The highly reduced plastome of T. angustimitra fits completely the general picture of plastome degradation in heterotrophic plants. Whereas the mitogenome in many aspects appears unaffected by the lifestyle, the recombinational activity is unusually low. Surprisingly, we find evidence of horizontal gene transfer, suggesting that this phenomenon may be more common among mycoheterotrophic plants than previously thought.

papers.title: Statistical shape model–based refinement of dental surface geometries for digital manufacturing workflows
papers.journal: The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology
papers.abstract: Abstract Digital manufacturing workflows in dentistry require accurate and anatomically consistent tooth models derived from heterogeneous acquisition modalities. However, preliminary tooth segmentations obtained from CBCT or intraoral scanning often exhibit incomplete or ambiguous regions, particularly at interdental contacts, which can compromise downstream design and manufacturing processes. This work presents a fully automated, anatomy-aware refinement pipeline based on an enhanced Statistical Shape Model, designed as a post-processing stage for preliminary tooth reconstructions. The method integrates target geometries with population-based anatomical priors, explicitly preserving reliable surface regions while reconstructing uncertain or missing areas through a globally constrained statistical deformation. Semantic anatomical information embedded in the eSSM enables contact-aware refinement relevant to design-oriented applications. The pipeline was evaluated on adult maxillary first molars using target models derived from both CBCT-based segmentations and intraoral scans. The results demonstrate that the proposed approach produces complete, smooth, and anatomically plausible tooth models while maintaining fidelity to the observed geometry. The refined reconstructions are directly suitable for downstream manufacturing-related applications, reducing manual intervention and improving robustness within digital dental workflows.

papers.title: Hz-resolution wide-span photonic integrated terahertz signal analyzer
papers.abstract: Wide-span spectral and noise characterization at millimeter-wave and terahertz frequencies is increasingly important for emerging wireless, sensing, and spectroscopy systems, yet remains challenging for conventional electronic instrumentation because of the complexity and calibration burden of extender-, multiplier-, and mixer-chain architectures. Here we show that photonics can provide attractive alternatives to this highly challenging electronic instrumentation through an antenna-coupled thin-film lithium niobate electro-optic receiver. Our implementation performs fast spectral reconstruction across the widely separated WR 9.0 (80-125 GHz) and WR 2.8 (240-380 GHz) bands with a single component, with carrier-frequency errors below 3 MHz, scan speeds up to 25 THz/s, and a displayed average noise level below -104 dBm/Hz. We then extend to Hz-level resolution and demonstrate phase-noise characterisation capabilities across these ultra-wide bands by using a mode-locked femtosecond-laser frequency comb as a sampling clock, mapping high-frequency carriers to aliased intermediate-frequency tones. We validate the method by measuring the phase noise of 90.225 GHz and 270.675 GHz carriers using the same chip and system configuration. We further improve the sensitivity of the phase-noise measurement through cross-correlation between two optical probe-pulse channels. Finally, we show that the same technique can be applied synchronously to ten widely spaced frequencies distributed across more than 100 GHz, with the option to quantify their mutual coherence. These results establish TFLN integrated photonics as a scalable route toward compact millimeter-wave/terahertz instrumentation.

papers.title: Automatic generation of exchange–correlation response kernels
papers.abstract: Computing density-functional response properties requires contracting derivatives of the exchange–correlation (xc) energy with perturbed densities on a grid. While the xc functional’s derivatives have long been available to high orders from libraries such as Libxc, the surrounding contraction layer—the chain rule that combines them with the grid-based basis-function and density data into the total xc contribution—has instead been hand-derived and hand-coded in every program, for every functional family, spin case, and property. We present libxckernel, a library that automatically generates this layer by symbolic differentiation. The xc functional’s ingredients are expressed as sesquilinear forms in the density matrix, so the xc energy can be differentiated to any order while the functional derivatives remain opaque. The basis functions and the orbital coefficients may both be complex. The chain rule then produces any xc matrix element: Fock matrices, orbital Hessians, or any other response terms of any order. Terms sharing a pattern are collapsed for efficiency. Extensible plugins emit the expressions as NumPy Einstein sums, compiled C++ kernels with C/Fortran interfaces, or host-program specific source code. libxckernel is free and open-source software under the BSD-3-Clause license, enabling rapid implementation of functionality missing from many electronic structure programs. We demonstrate it by extending Psi4 with meta-generalized gradient approximation (mGGA) response kernels for orbital stability analysis and time-dependent density-functional theory (TD-DFT), GGA and mGGA analytic nuclear Hessians, and exact quadrature grid response, as well as by extending GPAW with mGGA and triplet TD-DFT kernels and gradient-corrected kernels for periodic dielectric response.

papers.title: Evaluating nursing performance during heatwave simulations: Protocol for a repeated measures cross-over study
papers.abstract: Abstract This study protocol combines clinical simulations with climatic chamber experiments, to evaluate 1) the impact of heat stress on hospital nurses’ physiological strain, physical and mental fatigue, vigilance, and clinical performance; and 2) the efficacy of a practical cooling intervention (i.e. electric fan) in mitigating the negative impact of heat stress. UK-based, registered adult nurses working in hospital settings will be recruited to partake in a repeated-measures cross-over design study, consisting of five separate 3-hour experimental sessions simulating clinical work, and taking place within a climatic chamber at Southampton General Hospital (UK). Sessions will differ by ambient temperature and cooling intervention as follows: 1) control (CTR; 18°C, 50% relative humidity [RH]); 2) warm (WARM; 26°C, 50%RH); 3) warm with electric fan (WARM+FAN; 26°C, 50%RH); 4) hot (HOT; 34°C, 50%RH); 5) hot with electric fan (HOT+FAN; 34°C, 50%RH). This study has been registered on a publicly accessible clinical trial registry ( ISRCTN45793399 ). During each session, participants will first complete a standardised fatigue-induction protocol simulating shift work (i.e. low-intensity cycling with cognitive tasks); followed by a simulated hospital ward round involving six simulated patients and two simulated cardiac arrest scenarios. Nursing cognitive and physical performance will be assessed using a standardised observational assessment battery, along with objective cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) performance metrics. Physiological responses will be assessed by monitoring changes in core temperature (T core ), skin temperature (T skin ), heart rate, and whole-body sweat loss (WBSL). Fatigue and vigilance will be measured using the Swedish Occupational Fatigue Inventory (SOFI) and Brief Psychomotor Vigilance Task (PVT-B), respectively. Baseline (i.e. prior to fatiguing protocol) to post simulation changes in 1) vigilance assessed via the PVT-B (i.e. a determinant of role-specific cognitive performance); 2) CPR quality score (i.e. a determinant of role-specific physical performance); and 3) T core (i.e. a determinant of thermo-physiological state); will be analysed using linear mixed models to determine the effects of ambient temperature and cooling intervention on nurses’ clinical and physiological performance. By providing a controlled methodological framework for assessing the effects of heat exposure on hospital nurses’ physiological, perceptual, and clinical performance, this study will provide empirical evidence on air temperature-related changes in nursing performance and physiological strain and the role of cooling interventions in modifying these responses. This will support the development of evidence-based climate adaptation strategies to protect healthcare staff wellbeing and maintain patient safety during periods of extreme heat.

papers.title: Investigation of the microstructural and magnetic properties of Ni on GeSn layers
papers.journal: Journal of Physics D Applied Physics
papers.abstract: Abstract Thermal processing of nickel (Ni) layers on germanium–tin (GeSn) can strongly modify the Ni film and the Ni/GeSn interface within a restricted thermal budget; however, the influence of GeSn crystalline quality on Ni–Ge–Sn interfacial evolution and the magnetic response of the Ni layer remains incompletely understood. Here, Ni (15 nm)/Ge 1 − x Sn x /Ge/Gd 2 O 3 /Si(111) heterostructures ( x = 0.08 and 0.10 ) were investigated following rapid thermal annealing at 573 and 973 K for 10 s using x-ray diffraction, pole-figure analysis, x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy depth profiling, and temperature- and field-dependent magnetization measurements. Annealing at 573 K preserves the crystallographic texture of Ge 0.92 Sn 0.08 , whereas Ge 0.90 Sn 0.10 exhibits microtwin formation and reduced structural integrity. Annealing at 973 K, employed as a severe upper-bound thermal reference, causes extensive structural degradation in both heterostructures, with substantially greater deterioration in the higher-Sn sample. XPS depth profiling reveals progressive Ni–Ge–Sn intermixing accompanied by pronounced Sn surface segregation with increasing annealing temperature. Magnetization measurements show coexisting ferromagnetic and superparamagnetic contributions in the as-deposited and 573 K samples, whereas annealing at 973 K strongly suppresses the ferromagnetic response, producing highly unsaturated M ( H ) loops together with reduced saturation magnetization and coercivity. These magnetic changes are consistent with extensive interfacial alloying and dilution of the metallic Ni layer. This study establishes a direct correlation between GeSn crystalline quality, interfacial diffusion, and magnetic behavior.

Here, Ni (15 nm)/Ge 1 − x Sn x /Ge/Gd 2 O 3 /Si(111) heterostructures ( x = 0.08 and 0.10 ) were investigated following rapid thermal annealing at 573 and 973 K for 10 s using x-ray diffraction, pole-figure analysis, x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy depth profiling, and temperature- and field-dependent magnetization measurements. papers.title: Functional edible films and coatings enriched with flower extracts: advances in bioactivity and food preservation
papers.abstract: Although flower-derived bioactive compounds have gained attention as potential functional additives in edible packaging materials, no recent review has critically focused on their extraction strategies, interactions with film-forming biopolymers, and applications in food preservation. This review critically discusses recent research on the extraction, characterization, and application of important flower-derived bioactive compounds, including anthocyanins, flavonoids, phenolic acids, carotenoids, and essential oils, in active and intelligent edible packaging. Contemporary extraction techniques, such as ultrasound-assisted extraction, microwave-assisted extraction, deep eutectic solvents, and supercritical fluid CO 2 , provide higher yields (up to ~14 mg/g phenolics and over 70% pigment recovery) compared to traditional techniques. Nevertheless, each method has specific advantages and drawbacks. These flower-derived bioactive compounds modify the mechanical behavior and physicochemical characteristics of natural polymer-based packaging matrices, including starch, pectin, chitosan, and protein systems, mainly through hydrogen bonding and polyphenol–matrix interactions. Active films show improved oxidative stability. Antioxidant activity may increase two fold to tenfold, while antimicrobial action can reduce microbial load by approximately 1–3 log CFU/g. Moreover, the mechanical response to these compounds depends on extract–matrix compatibility, with phenolic compounds acting either as plasticizing or strengthening components depending on the polymer system and concentration. Anthocyanin-rich flower extracts from hibiscus and butterfly pea provide pH-responsive color-changing behavior, making these intelligent packaging systems capable of tracking food spoilage. Food applications show shelf-life extension of 5–21 days in fruits, vegetables, and meat systems, mainly through antioxidant activity, antimicrobial effects, delayed oxidative deterioration, reduced microbial growth, and improved moisture regulation. In contrast, biodegradability and renewable biopolymer use should be viewed as sustainability advantages rather than direct preservation mechanisms. However, wider application of flower-extract-based edible films still requires further validation of scale-up feasibility, food-contact regulatory approval, migration behavior, sensory acceptability, and safety of released bioactive compounds.

papers.title: Enhancement mechanism of high temperature stability for in-situ oxide scale on high-entropy carbide coatings induced by rare earth
papers.abstract: Abstract For ultra-high temperature ceramic (UHTC) coatings used in aerospace thermal protection systems, enhancing the oxygen barrier capability and thermal stability of in-situ oxide scale during ablation is crucial for stable service. Herein, a high-entropy design strategy is proposed to boost the compactness and phase stability of oxide scales by leveraging multi-component synergistic effects. Three high-entropy carbide coatings, (Hf-Zr-Ti-Sc-Y-Sm)C (HEC-Sm), (Hf-Zr-Ti-Sc-Y-Er)C (HEC-Er) and (Hf-Zr-Ti-Sc-Y-Lu)C (HEC-Lu), with better ablation resistance than ZrC, (Hf-Zr-Ti)C, and (Hf-Zr-Ti-Sc-Y)C coatings,were designed. HEC-Lu delivers optimal ablation resistance, featuring a linear ablation rate of -0.173 ± 0.012 μm·s-1, superior to HEC-Sm (-0.111 ± 0.032 μm·s-1) and HEC-Er (-0.144 ± 0.022 μm·s-1). This superior performance is correlated with higher Ti retention and stronger calculated Ti-O bonding, increasing Ti content in the oxide scale by 53.85 % and 33.33 % compared to HEC-Sm and HEC-Er, thereby inhibiting volatilization. Rare-earth (Sm, Er, Lu) incorporation can reduce the diffusion coefficients of Ti and O atoms in oxide scales by one order of magnitude at 2573 K compared with TiO2. Notably, Lu introducing yields a higher Mulliken population (0.279) for Ti-O bonds than that of Sm (0.268) and Er (0.274), which strengthens Ti-O bonds inside the oxide scale. This work presents a novel material selection scheme for anti-ablation coatings in extreme environments.

papers.title: Biomass to bioenergy transition through sustainable bioconversion and circular bioeconomy strategies
papers.abstract: Access to modern electricity and clean cooking technologies remains uneven across much of Africa, despite the continent's abundant biomass resources, which have the potential to enhance energy security while supporting the transition toward a circular bioeconomy. However, a substantial proportion of agricultural, forestry, municipal, and marine organic residues is still treated as waste rather than valorized within the formal energy sector. Morocco exemplifies this disconnect. Although the country has achieved near-universal rural electrification, biomass derived from agricultural and marine resources contributes less than 2% of the modern energy mix, highlighting that the principal challenge lies not in resource availability but in the development of efficient conversion pathways and integrated deployment strategies. This review examines recent advances in biomass-to-bioenergy technologies, with particular emphasis on sustainable bioconversion processes, including enzymatic hydrolysis, microbial fermentation, anaerobic digestion, and microbial fuel cells. Beyond evaluating technological progress, we assess research trends, innovation dynamics, and technology transfer through bibliometric and patent analyses to identify leading research areas, emerging technologies, and geographical disparities across Africa. We further discuss the role of life cycle assessment in evaluating the environmental sustainability of biomass conversion pathways and demonstrate its importance in identifying low-carbon alternatives capable of reducing greenhouse gas emissions. We conclude that Africa's energy sovereignty depends on moving away from generic policies toward integrated, country-specific deployment strategies that prioritize locally available biomass within circular bioeconomy frameworks.
