papers.title: Baculovirus-Mediated Expression and Functional Characterization of a Glycyrrhizin-Specific Single-Chain Variable Fragment in Sf9 Cells
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Glycyrrhizin (GC) is a major bioactive saponin in licorice plants ( Glycyrrhiza spp.). A GC-specific single-chain variable fragment (GC-scFv) was constructed from anti-GC monoclonal antibody 2H2. To obtain a soluble recombinant recognition reagent for GC immunoassays, GC-scFv was expressed using a baculovirus–insect cell platform. Methods The variable heavy- and light-chain genes were amplified from 2H2 hybridoma-derived complementary DNA (cDNA) and assembled using a (Gly 4 Ser) 3 linker. The construct was transferred through pET-28a(+) and pCold I into pFastBac1Mel, which contains the honeybee melittin signal sequence for secretion in Sf9 insect cells. GC-scFv was recovered by nickel-chelate affinity chromatography and characterized using indirect competitive enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (icELISA). The calibration curve was analyzed by semi-logarithmic regression using triplicate wells at each concentration. Results An anti-T7-tag Western blot detected GC-scFv at approximately 29 kDa in the eluate recovered from culture medium. Free GC produced concentration-dependent inhibition, with a half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC 50 ) of 0.46 μg/mL and a semi-logarithmic calibration interval of 0.0488–3.125 μg/mL. The apparent limit of detection and apparent limit of quantification, defined as 10% and 20% inhibition, were 54.2 and 92.8 ng/mL, respectively. Cross-reactivity was 24.47% toward glycyrrhetinic acid 3- O -glucuronide, 6.52% toward glycyrrhetinic acid, and below 0.92% toward the remaining tested compounds. Conclusions The baculovirus–Sf9 platform produced GC-scFv with competitive binding activity toward GC. The recovered reagent and its assay characteristics provide a basis for developing recombinant antibody-based immunoassays for licorice-containing products.

papers.title: Pregnancy Risk Information Systems for Psychotropic Medications: A Practical Review for Clinical Decision-Making
papers.abstract: Objective This review aimed to summarize pregnancy risk information systems for psychotropic medications and recent evidence on reproductive safety, with the goal of improving clinicians’ awareness of drug-specific risk information relevant to individualized clinical decision- making in women with psychiatric disorders of reproductive age.Methods We narratively reviewed official reproductive safety information resources from Australia, Europe, Korea, the United Kingdom, and the United States, together with recent umbrella-review evidence on psychotropic medication safety during pregnancy. Information on selected agents was organized by drug class.Results National systems differed in structure and clinical utility. Australia and Korea retain category-based elements, whereas sources from Europe, the United Kingdom, and the United States provide more descriptive, context-based information. Antipsychotics were mainly associated with neonatal extrapyramidal or withdrawal symptoms and metabolic risk signals for selected agents. Mood stabilizers and anticonvulsants were more strongly associated with congenital malformations and neurodevelopmental disorders. Benzodiazepines and hypnotics were mainly associated with neonatal sedation, respiratory depression, hypotonia, feeding difficulties, and withdrawal symptoms after late-pregnancy or labor exposure. Antidepressants were associated with neonatal adaptation symptoms, persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn, and postpartum hemorrhage. Recent umbrella-review evidence showed that most reported associations remained at suggestive or weak levels of evidence.Conclusion Psychotropic medication use during pregnancy should be guided by individualized risk–benefit assessment, integrating drug-specific safety signals, evidence quality, exposure timing, lactation and fertility considerations, and the risks of untreated psychiatric illness.

papers.title: Prevalence and Intervention Gaps for PTSD and CPTSD Following Interpersonal Trauma in Low- and Middle-Income Countries: A Systematic Review
papers.abstract: Objective The psychological burden of interpersonal trauma is a significant global concern, yet a critical gap remains in identifying and treating trauma-related disorders in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Following the introduction of the International Classification of Diseases 11th Revision (ICD-11), understanding the distinction between post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and complex PTSD (CPTSD) has become essential, particularly in resource-constrained settings where chronic trauma is prevalent.Methods We conducted a systematic review following PRISMA guidelines to examine prevalence of interpersonal trauma, PTSD/CPTSD prevalence, and available interventions in LMICs. Thirty-five studies were selected following independent data extraction and quality appraisal by two reviewers based on JBI Critical Appraisal and Cochrane Risk of Bias assessments.Results The findings indicate a substantial gap between high interpersonal trauma exposure and clinical recognition. Children, adolescents, and women were identified as the most vulnerable populations, frequently exposed to domestic and gender-based violence. While PTSD prevalence rates were high across LMICs, only three studies utilized the ICD-11 criteria for CPTSD. Regarding interventions, while evidence-based models such as trauma-focused cognitive behavioral therapy and narrative exposure therapy have been implemented, evaluation research in LMICs remains limited compared to the high trauma burden.Conclusion This review highlights a diagnostic lag and research-to-practice gap in LMICs, particularly concerning the CPTSD recently introduced in ICD-11. Addressing these disparities requires prioritizing implementation science frameworks, focusing on task-shifting models, cultural tailoring of evidence-based interventions, and the integration of digital health solutions to ensure sustainable care for vulnerable survivors.

papers.title: A biosynthetic paradox implicating dynamic zeaxanthin biosynthesis at the ER-LD interface
papers.abstract: Traditional metabolic engineering often treats lipid droplets (LDs) as inert storage sinks and assumes shortening enzyme-substrate distance inherently enhances pathway efficiency. Harnessing Yarrowia lipolytica for zeaxanthin production, we uncovered a pivotal “spatial paradox” challenging this conventional dogma. A selective shielding strategy first identified the hydroxylase Pa CrtZ as the primary biosynthetic bottleneck. Subcellular localization trials revealed that directly targeting Pa CrtZ to the β-carotene-rich LD surface unexpectedly yielded the lowest zeaxanthin relative fraction (9.87%), significantly underperforming compared to cytosolic (27.15%) or peroxisomal targeting (43.16%). To investigate this counterintuitive phenomenon, multidimensional engineering strategies were implemented to boost zeaxanthin accumulation. Subsequently, in situ , label-free stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) microscopy unequivocally demonstrated the co-localization of β-carotene and zeaxanthin within LDs, confirming that substrate inaccessibility was not the limiting factor. Guided by principles of LD biogenesis, these findings led us to conceptualize a dynamic endoplasmic reticulum (ER)–LD interface functional microenvironment model. We propose that robust Pa CrtZ-catalyzed hydroxylation is sustained predominantly at transient ER–LD junctions, where hydrophobic β-carotene "skimming" is dynamically synchronized with efficient O 2 and NADPH cofactor exchange. This model redefines lipid organelles as active, organized metabolic hubs beyond mere storage, offering a novel transformative framework for future organelle-targeted metabolic interface design.

papers.title: Terbium-Doped Graphene Quantum Dots: A Highly Efficient and Selective Fluorescent Nanoprobe for Vanillin Detection
papers.abstract: Abstract Vanillin, an extensively used flavoring compound in our daily life, may lead to health problems when overused, adulterated, or poorly controlled in commercial settings, necessitating the development of sensitive and rapid detection techniques. In this work, terbium-doped graphene quantum dots (Tb-GQD) were synthesized using carbonization and chemical conjugation methods for developing an efficient fluorescent probe for vanillin detection. The structural and optical characteristics of Tb-GQD confirm that terbium is doped in GQDs, without disturbing the sp2 graphitic core of GQD, and efficient energy transfer from GQD to Tb3+ was observed from the photoluminescence emission studies. Upon addition of vanillin to Tb-GQD, a decrease in fluorescence emission intensity and a change in lifetime were observed, suggesting a dynamic, photoinduced electron transfer mechanism. The Tb-GQD shows a linear detection range of 0.2–85 μM with a detection limit of 13.2 nM. The synthesized fluorescent probe shows excellent selectivity, and was implemented in real-sample analysis with a good recovery range of 96.4–100.06% and an RSD below 3.6%. These findings show that Tb-GQD will serve as an efficient platform for detecting vanillin.

papers.title: Advances in Wire-Laser Metal Deposition: Bimetallic Fabrication, Defect Mitigation, and Future Directions
papers.journal: Lasers in Manufacturing and Materials Processing
papers.abstract: Abstract Wire-Laser Metal Deposition (W-LMD) is a transformative additive manufacturing technology that utilizes a laser heat source to melt metallic wire feedstock for the high-efficiency fabrication of large-scale, near-net-shape components. The technology is distinguished from other manufacturing processes due to its high material utilization efficiency and superior safety compared to metal powder-based systems. W-LMD systems are composed of a focused laser, a wire feeder mechanism, a multi-degree of freedom motion system, cooling system, and a shielding gas supply to prevent oxidation. Deviation in process parameters of the system components can lead to external defects such as stubbing (insufficient melting) and dripping (melting above the melt pool), or other forms of internal defects such as porosities. A key feature of W-LMD systems is their capability of fabricating bimetallic structures. This paper reviews key studies on W-LMD systems and their advancements in bimetallic fabrication. The review highlights the current gaps and required research work in the field for bimetallic W-LMD manufacturing and its significance.

papers.title: Evaluation of recovered Carbon black as a sustainable alternative to commercial Carbon black in solid tyre cushion compounds
authors: D. M. D. A. De Zoysa
papers.abstract: Pyrolysis is a sustainable solution for waste tyre (WT) management. Recovered carbon black (rCB), is a second highest by-product of tyre pyrolysis process, contains a high amount of carbon, ash and inorganic impurities. In the present study, rCB derived from WTs was upgraded through magnetic separation, ball milling, and purified treating twice with 2M HCl and once with 2M NaOH at 60⁰C for one hour using 2 g/mL rCB: leachate ratio to obtain demineralized rCB(drCB). Both raw rCB and drCB were characterized by particle size analysis, proximate and ultimate analyses, TGA, ICP-OES, FT-IR, XRD, and iodine adsorption. The drCB exhibited a substantial reduction in ash content from 22.20% to 3.42 % (by weight) and an increase in carbon content up to 94.41 % (% wt). The upgraded drCB was subsequently incorporated into solid tyre cushion compounds as a partial replacement for commercial carbon black (CCB, N550) to evaluate industrial feasibility. Physico-mechanical properties of the drCB compound demonstrated improved modulus, tear strength, hardness, and other properties such as tensile strength, rebound resilience within the industrial standard limits. These findings confirm the technical feasibility of rCB as a partial replacement of the filler in industrial solid tyre cushion compounds, supporting circular economy concept in the rubber and tyre industry.

papers.title: Preformulation Study of Aqueous Extracts of Avocado (Persea americana Mill.) Seed from Criollo and Hass Cultivars for Solid Dosage Forms
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Avocado (Persea americana Mill.) seed is an agro-industrial by-product with significant pharmacological potential. This study aimed to conduct a preformulation assessment of aqueous seed extracts from Criollo (M1) and Hass (M2) cultivars. Methods: The extracts were characterized for total phenolic content (TPC) and ABTS•+ scavenging capacity, and their compatibility with pharmaceutical excipients was evaluated in binary mixtures by Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy with Pearson correlation and hierarchical cluster analysis (HCA), differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), and isothermal stress testing (50 °C, 15 days) with HPLC quantification of epicatechin (IST-HPLC). Results: M2 showed significantly higher TPC (192.80 ± 4.90 µg GAE/mg) than M1 (27.08 ± 0.51 µg GAE/mg; p < 0.0001). ABTS•+ inhibition was 59.92 ± 1.76% for M1 (0.05 mg/mL) and 50.79 ± 1.19% for M2 (0.01 mg/mL). The DSC transition enthalpies of both extracts did not differ significantly (p = 0.1271). Maltodextrin and gum arabic were compatible with both extracts, suggesting that they could serve as common excipients for both cultivars, whereas the chemical stability of five M2 mixtures could not be determined by IST-HPLC. Sodium carboxymethylcellulose (CMC) was incompatible with M1, as shown by a 29.44 percentage-point decrease in epicatechin recovery (p < 0.0001), separate HCA clustering (Euclidean distance > 0.009), and the lowest FTIR spectral correlation (r = 0.990). Conclusions: These findings provide a scientific basis for the rational development of solid dosage forms from avocado seed extracts.

papers.title: Proving That a GPU, NPU, DPU or Other Device Consumed the Intended Command, Used Current Memory Translations and Produced Only the Declared Effect
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: AI workloads reach hardware through runtimes, drivers, command queues, firmware and IOMMU/SMMU translations before a GPU, NPU, DPU or other device produces an effect. Permission to compute, driver acceptance, a descriptor that was inspected a moment ago and the host’s current page tables do not prove what the device actually did. A descriptor can change after it was checked; a stale IOTLB entry can direct DMA to the wrong page; a reset or firmware update can reuse a queue slot for another tenant; a replayed command can be consumed twice; and a SmartNIC or peer-to-peer path can produce a network or storage effect that no one authorized. This disclosure describes a vendor-neutral, non-actuating method for reconstructing silicon-level consistency from evidence. Each hardware command is bound to an original operation, principal and permitted class. The descriptor the device actually consumes is compared by digest with the approved one. Queue, mapping, firmware and device-incarnation generations must be current; DMA bounds and permissions must hold; translation invalidation must be acknowledged; admission must cover every effect path and be replay-safe; and device completion and the observed effect must correspond to the original operation. Results are combined in three-valued logic: a proven contradiction yields CONTRADICTED even when other evidence is missing, full support yields SUPPORTED, and gaps yield UNRESOLVED — in particular, missing effect telemetry is never treated as proof that no effect occurred. The document provides a 60-stage, six-phase silicon workflow and a separate 60-stage integratedembodiment, each with flowcharts, 72 technical invariants, twelve hardware variations (GPU, DPU/SmartNIC, CPU trusted domains, chiplets, firmware, peripherals), 48 formal relations, 60 engineering checkpoints, a comparison with existing mechanisms (IOMMU/SMMU and ATS invalidation, PCIe IDE and TDISP, confidential-computing device assignment, SR-IOV and function-level reset, doorbell and queue protections, device attestation with SPDM, GPU command validation and DPU offload) and anon-actuating reference evaluator in Python, JavaScript and Go with 90 shared synthetic vectors, all passing. It is not hardware-validated or certified; the laboratory is synthetic, self-authored and not peer reviewed. The author is open to acquihire or strategic collaboration. Keywords: AI safety; hardware security; GPU; NPU; DPU; SmartNIC; command descriptors; DMA; IOMMU; SMMU; IOTLB invalidation; ATS; TOCTOU; device reset; function-level reset; device incarnation; firmware update; replay prevention; PCIe IDE; TDISP; SPDM attestation; confidential computing; three-valued logic

papers.title: Artificial intelligence assisted multiobjective design of functionally graded materials using hybrid optimization and experimental validation
papers.abstract: Designing functionally graded materials (FGMs) through conventional trial-and-error approaches is time-intensive and difficult to scale for large multi-material design spaces. This study presents an AI-assisted, computational-intelligence-based framework for compatibility-aware material selection and gradient-profile optimization of FGM structures. The framework combines a curated database of 180 candidate materials with a mixed-variable hybrid genetic algorithm–particle swarm optimization approach to balance weight, cost, stiffness, strength, and thermal resistance. Rapid objective-function screening was followed by finite element verification of shortlisted designs and proof-of-concept experimental validation using powder-metallurgy-fabricated Al₂O₃/Ti-6Al-4V FGM beam specimens. For the representative beam case considered, the optimized FGM showed approximately 25% lower weight, 30% lower deflection, corresponding to approximately 43% higher effective stiffness under identical loading, and 60% lower peak thermal stress compared with the corresponding homogeneous reference under the same modeling assumptions. Experimental measurements from three specimens showed differences of approximately 3% for elastic modulus and 4% for ultimate strength relative to numerical predictions, supporting the feasibility of the workflow for the present case while indicating the need for broader statistical validation. The estimated per-design screening and verification time decreased from approximately 480 h for a conventional trial-and-error route to approximately 18 h after database preparation, although this comparison is case-specific and depends on model fidelity, hardware, and available material data. Overall, the results suggest that AI-assisted multi-objective optimization can serve as a useful decision-support tool for narrowing FGM design spaces before detailed numerical and experimental qualification.

papers.title: Thermally Conductive Enhanced Composite Phase Change Materials for Improving Thermal Safety of Lithium-Ion Batteries
papers.abstract: Thermal runaway of lithium-ion batteries is a critical issue restricting their safe application. Efficient thermal management and flame-retardant protection are essential for improving the safety of battery systems. In this study, polyethylene glycol (PEG) was used as the phase change energy storage matrix, and expanded graphite (EG), flake copper, and MXene nanosheets were introduced to construct a three-dimensional thermally conductive enhancement network. Zinc hydroxystannate (ZHS) and ammonium polyphosphate (APP) were added as synergistic flame retardants to prepare thermally conductive enhanced composite phase change materials with efficient heat dissipation, leakage prevention, and flame retardancy. The structure and thermal properties of the materials were systematically characterized by XRD, SEM, DSC, TGA, and the steady-state heat flow method, with emphasis on evaluating their thermal safety regulation performance in lithium-ion battery cells and modules. The results show that the composite PCMs exhibit no leakage at 60 °C and 80 °C, and the thermal conductivity reaches 3.81 W/(m·K) at a metal filler mass fraction of 20%. In module tests at a 3C discharge rate, the CM2 material reduced the peak temperature by 25.2 °C compared with natural cooling and maintained the maximum temperature difference between cells within the safety threshold. In addition, the inherent flame retardancy of the material helps delay thermal runaway propagation, providing dual safety protection through heat dissipation and fire resistance for battery systems. This study offers a new approach for the design of high-safety thermal management materials for lithium-ion batteries.

papers.title: Preoperative prognostic nutritional index, opioid-sparing anesthesia, and outcomes after gynecologic cancer surgery: a retrospective cohort study
papers.abstract: Background Preoperative prognostic nutritional index (PNI) may identify patients at increased perioperative risk, but whether PNI is associated with differences in outcomes across anesthetic strategies remains uncertain. Methods This retrospective cohort included 342 women undergoing surgery for ovarian, endometrial, or cervical cancer from 2019 to 2024. PNI was calculated as serum albumin (g/L) + 5 × absolute lymphocyte count (10 9 /L); PNI < 45 was used as a prespecified pragmatic cutoff. A propofol-based total intravenous, opioid-sparing multimodal strategy, with regional or neuraxial analgesia when feasible, was compared with volatile-based anesthesia and opioid-centered analgesia. Outcomes included postoperative biomarkers, 30-day complications, return to intended oncologic therapy (RIOT) within 42 days, recurrence-free survival (RFS), and overall survival (OS). Regression models examined PNI-by-strategy interactions. Results PNI < 45 was present in 156/342 patients (45.6%). Within this stratum, median postoperative day 3 CRP was 79.1 vs. 92.6 mg/L, major complications occurred in 18.8% vs. 43.3%, and timely RIOT occurred in 79.1% vs. 55.4% with opioid-sparing vs. conventional anesthesia, respectively. Reported 36-month RFS estimates were 72.8% vs. 36.5%. In the cancer-type-stratified adjusted Cox model, the low-PNI term in the conventional-anesthesia reference stratum was associated with RFS (adjusted HR 2.14, 95% CI 1.31–3.48), with a nominal PNI-by-strategy interaction for RFS (interaction HR 0.46, 95% CI 0.22–0.94; p = 0.033). The interaction was not significant for OS ( p = 0.837) or after changing the PNI cutoff to 44 or 46. Conclusions Lower PNI was associated with greater perioperative and oncologic risk. The observed RFS interaction is exploratory and sensitive to PNI dichotomization; residual oncologic, procedural, and calendar-era confounding precludes causal interpretation. Prospective confirmation with continuous PNI modeling and detailed cancer-specific adjustment is required.

papers.title: Characterization of Torrefied Waste Hops for Bioenergy Applications: Moisture Sorption Kinetics and Thermal Analysis
papers.abstract: Biomass is a promising renewable energy source; however, its direct use is limited by high hygroscopicity, low energy density, and challenging storage conditions. This study investigated the effect of thermal pretreatment temperature on the moisture sorption behavior and thermal stability of waste hops. Waste hops were torrefied at 250 °C, 350 °C, and 450 °C. Equilibrium moisture content (EMC) was measured at 30 °C under three relative humidity levels (50%, 70%, and 80%). The sorption data were fitted using four empirical models (Henderson, Chung-Pfost, Halsey, and Oswin), and model performance was evaluated using statistical parameters (R2, RMSE, RSS). Structural and compositional changes were analyzed by thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), and elemental and proximate analyses. For untreated hops, the Halsey and Oswin models described the data almost exactly (R2 ≥ 0.999), while the Halsey model was the most suitable for samples torrefied at 250 °C and 350 °C (R2 = 0.991 and 0.951, respectively). For the sample torrefied at 450 °C, none of the models provided an adequate fit. As the material became less hygroscopic, the agreement of all four models decreased (R2 of the best model from 1.000 for WH-raw to < 0.77 for WH-450). Because only three relative humidity levels were measured, the model ranking should be regarded as indicative. At 80% RH, torrefaction at 250 °C, 350 °C and 450 °C reduced the EMC by 30%, 50% and 64%, respectively, compared with that of the untreated material. With increasing torrefaction temperature, the onset decomposition temperature increased from 212.5 °C (WH-raw) to 412.3 °C (WH-450), and the final decomposition temperature from 512.9 °C to 581.4 °C. The improvement in hygroscopic and thermal stability with torrefaction temperature was not linear: the additional reduction in EMC became smaller at higher temperatures, and the higher heating value increased mainly between 250 and 350 °C, with only a marginal further gain at 450 °C. Total mass loss decreased from 77.11% to 39.77%, while the solid residue at 900 °C increased from 22.89% to 60.23%. FTIR spectra indicated degradation of hydrophilic functional groups. Thermal pretreatment improved the hydrophobicity and thermal stability of waste hops. The validated sorption models offer a useful tool for optimizing drying and storage conditions, enhancing the potential of waste hops as a sustainable bioenergy feedstock.

papers.title: Co-Processed Corn Starch (Zea mays L.) as a Novel Pharmaceutical Excipient: Development and Physicochemical Characterization
papers.abstract: Corn starch (Zea mays L.) is widely used as a pharmaceutical excipient because of its biocompatibility, biodegradability, and non-toxicity. However, its application is limited by poor flow properties, low water solubility, and a tendency toward retrogradation, which may reduce its effectiveness in solid dosage formulations. Although pregelatinization has been used to improve starch functionality, studies on the combined application of pregelatinization and co-processing with sodium starch glycolate (SSG) remain limited. Therefore, this study aimed to develop and characterize co-processed pregelatinized corn starch as a novel pharmaceutical excipient. Pregelatinized corn starch (PCS) was prepared and co-processed with SSG at ratios of 1:1, 1:2, and 1:3 (g/g). The resulting powders were characterized using X-ray diffraction (XRD), differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and particle size analysis (PSA). Powder properties, including flow rate, angle of repose, moisture content, and bulk density, were also evaluated. The co-processed formulations exhibited diffraction peaks at approximately 23°, indicating structural modification. DSC analysis showed enhanced thermal stability, with transition temperatures ranging from 63.78 °C to 96.50 °C. FTIR confirmed physical interactions without the formation of new chemical bonds. The flow rate increased from 0.472 g/s in native corn starch to 3.852 g/s in F3, while the angle of repose decreased from 37.38° to 24.1° in F1. Overall, co-processing improved the physicochemical and functional properties of corn starch, demonstrating its potential as a multifunctional pharmaceutical excipient for solid dosage forms.

DSC analysis showed enhanced thermal stability, with transition temperatures ranging from 63.78 °C to 96.50 °C.

papers.title: Development and optimisation of carbon enriched natural fibre hybrid composites and their characterisation for sustainable applications
papers.journal: Plastics Rubber and Composites Macromolecular Engineering
papers.abstract: Growing environmental concerns and the increasing demand for sustainable materials have accelerated the development of bio-based hybrid composites as alternatives to conventional synthetic composites. In this study, fully bio-based hybrid composites reinforced with sugarcane bagasse fibres and bamboo charcoal were fabricated using polylactic acid (PLA) matrix by varying the proportions of the reinforcements to identify the optimum composition. Scanning Electron Micrographs revealed the influence of reinforcement composition on fibre–matrix interfacial bonding and fracture morphology while Fourier Transform Infrared analysis confirmed the presence of characteristic functional groups associated with cellulose, hemicellulose and lignin. Thermogravimetric and derivative thermogravimetric analysis revealed enhanced thermal stability with primary degradation occurring between 250 and 450°C and maximum degradation temperature was recorded at 315°C. Among the investigated formulations, the B/BC (30/70) composite exhibited the best overall mechanical performance, achieving a tensile strength of 10.21 MPa, flexural strength of 79 MPa and an impact strength of 0.73 J/m 2 , owing to the synergistic interaction between sugarcane bagasse fibres and bamboo charcoal. In addition, the composites exhibited controlled moisture absorption behaviour that followed classical Fickian diffusion kinetics, indicating diffusion-controlled water transport. The combination of enhanced mechanical properties, good thermal stability, controlled moisture absorption and the utilisation of renewable agricultural waste materials demonstrated the potential of the developed hybrid composites as lightweight, biodegradable materials for non-structural applications such as packaging, horticultural products, decorative panels and low-stress consumer products with additional potential for adsorption-oriented applications.

papers.title: Boronic acid-functionalized graphene aerogels for selective catechol removal in complex multicomponent phenolic aerosols
papers.abstract: Selective adsorption in complex multicomponent aerosols remains challenging because structurally similar molecules often compete for identical adsorption sites. Herein, a boronic acid-functionalized three-dimensional graphene aerogel was developed as a selective adsorbent for phenolic compounds. Following 1,2-benzenediboronic acid modification, the specific surface area of graphene aerogel increased from 380.69 to 539.88 m 2 g −1 . In dynamic multicomponent aerosol experiments, the detected catechol amounts after filtration through B-14/CA and B-18/CA were 65.94 and 65.21 μg/cig, respectively, compared with 106.13 μg/cig for the conventional cellulose acetate filter. Other representative phenolic compounds exhibited responses distinct from that of catechol, demonstrating differential filtration in the competitive system. Density functional theory calculations showed that the optimized catechol complex did not correspond to a conventional boronate ester. Instead, a noncovalent B···O contact of approximately 2.06 Å closed a seven-membered pseudo-cyclic adsorption configuration without dehydration. The similar adsorption energies of catechol and guaiacol, −0.34319 and −0.34799 eV, respectively, indicated that a single optimized adsorption energy was insufficient to explain the experimental difference. These results suggest that the combination of hierarchical porous transport and configuration-dependent noncovalent recognition contributes to preferential catechol retention in multicomponent aerosols.

These results suggest that the combination of hierarchical porous transport and configuration-dependent noncovalent recognition contributes to preferential catechol retention in multicomponent aerosols.

papers.title: LARU-net: lesion-aware residual attention U-net for binary cucumber leaf lesion segmentation and continuous severity estimation
papers.abstract: Plant leaf diseases threaten agricultural productivity and motivate accurate automated monitoring. This study presents LARU-Net, a unified architecture for binary cucumber lesion segmentation (lesion versus background) with an auxiliary continuous severity-regression output on a bounded 0–4 scale. The network integrates a Disease Feature Enhancement Autoencoder, Residual Multi-Scale Encoder, transformer bottleneck, Attention-Guided Decoder, and Boundary Refinement Module. On the declared held-out test partition (1,080 images), the archived full-model results were Dice 0.9230, IoU 0.8660, Boundary F1 0.9350, and precision 0.9460; the previously emphasized Dice value of 0.9456 is a validation value and is now identified as such. Severity estimates yielded an overall MAE of 0.29, RMSE of 0.37, and R 2 of 0.90. These values are single-run point estimates from one greenhouse image collection. Plant/session identifiers, complete acquisition and annotation provenance, repeated-run logs, and an external dataset were not preserved in the supplied study archive; therefore, the results support in-domain evaluation but not broad cross-greenhouse or cross-season generalization. The split was stratified at image level; independence at plant, leaf, or acquisition-session level could not be verified. Confidence intervals and significance tests were not reconstructed because per-image predictions and repeated-run logs were unavailable.

papers.title: Sustainable Self-Healing Electrospun Fibers Enabled by Upcycled TPEE/PCL Blends through Dynamic Chain Mobility
papers.abstract: Abstract Upcycling polymer waste into functional fibrous materials is attractive for sustainable materials development, but a fundamental challenge remains: electrospun fibrous structures are highly susceptible to damage, while healing processes based on chain diffusion often induce structural collapse, loss of interfiber connectivity, and deterioration of mechanical performance. Here, we address this issue by developing an upcycled thermoplastic polyester elastomer (TPEE)/polycaprolactone (PCL) electrospun fibrous system that balances structural integrity with dynamic healing capability. In this design, the mechanically supportive TPEE framework helps retain fibrous features in selected blend compositions, while the semicrystalline PCL phase provides thermally responsive domains that promote segmental motion and interfacial chain diffusion under mild heating. This cooperative structure enables effective intrinsic self-healing without external healing agents or complex chemical modification while minimizing collapse of the fibrous network during repair. The results reveal a composition-dependent interplay between healing efficiency and mechanical robustness, demonstrating that controlled integration of a supportive elastic matrix with a reversible thermally active phase provides an effective strategy for extending the functional lifetime of upcycled fibrous materials.

papers.title: Epoxy and Vinyl Silane Functionalization of Graphene Nanoplatelets
papers.abstract: Abstract Functionalization of low-oxygen-content graphene nanoplatelets (GNP; C/O > 9:1) remains challenging due to the need to preserve the intrinsic transport properties associated with their high sp2 carbon content. Silanization provides an effective route to introduce reactive surface functionalities via hydrolysis–condensation reactions with surface hydroxyl groups. Here, the successful functionalization of GNP using vinyltrimethoxysilane (VTMS) and 3-glycidoxypropyltrimethoxysilane (G-PTMS) was achieved via a condensation silanization reaction or a pathway dependent on the R-group of each silane. Comprehensive characterization including X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), Raman spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction (XRD), electron microscopy, and thermogravimetric analysis coupled with mass spectrometry (TGA-MS) confirmed successful grafting of the silane species. This approach demonstrates that silanization is a viable and versatile strategy for functionalizing GNPs with reactive vinyl and epoxy functionalities which are then available for cross-linking with polymers and other substrates.

papers.title: PVC Cable Burning Behaviour and Intumescent Protection: Small-Scale Tests and the Browns Ferry Lesson
papers.journal: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
papers.abstract: Electrical cables are present in nearly every building and industrial site. In a fire they can act as the starting point, as a path along which flames travel, and as a major producer of smoke. This paper presents laboratory results for a single-core PVCinsulated copper cable and a literature review of passive fire protection (PFP), with attention to intumescent coatings. Two standard tests were run: vertical flame propagation under IEC 60332-1-2, and cone calorimetry at 40 kW/m² under ISO 5660-1. Both vertical specimens passed. Flames died out within 5 s of removing the burner, and charring reached only 80 mm and 160 mm along a 600 mm length. In the cone calorimeter the insulation ignited at 125 s, peaked at 114.89 kW/m², gave a total heat release of 70.81 MJ/m² and a smoke production rate of 0.175 m²/s. The material therefore shrugs off a small flame but, under sustained radiant heating, becomes a long-lived source of heat and smoke. The review part explains how intumescent coatings function, the product families available, how they fail, and how the 1975 Browns Ferry fire reshaped cable-protection rules.

papers.title: Leg glucose uptake and substrate utilisation during time trial exercise: Effects of acute hypobaric hypoxia and biological sex
papers.abstract: Abstract Hypoxia reduces exercise performance, yet it remains unclear how biological sex and altitude influence substrate utilisation during prolonged maximal exercise. Twenty‐two trained cyclists and triathletes (10 females) completed 30 min time trials (TTs) at low altitude (normoxia; ∼400 m) and moderate altitude (hypoxia; ∼2800 m in a hypobaric chamber) in counterbalanced order. Whole‐body metabolism was estimated from indirect calorimetry, whereas leg glucose uptake and substrate utilisation were derived from arterial and femoral venous blood samples and leg blood flow (thermodilution). Muscle biopsies were obtained from vastus lateralis to measure glycogen utilisation. Across altitudes, females displayed a higher fractional utilisation of during the TTs. TT performance was decreased in hypoxia, and the proportional decrease was smaller in females (−14%) than in males (−18%). Whole‐body substrate utilisation was similar between sexes in normoxia. However, males showed a large decrease in carbohydrate oxidation in hypoxia, whereas females displayed only a modest decrease. Males and females had similar leg metabolic responses to hypoxia: estimated glycogen oxidation decreased, with no change in absolute fat or blood glucose oxidation. However, across altitudes, females showed greater carbohydrate contributions, originating primarily from blood glucose rather than muscle glycogen. Estimates of fat contribution were uncertain but suggested a lower contribution in females than in males. In conclusion, females exercised at a higher relative intensity and derived relatively more energy from blood glucose. Males and females had similar leg metabolic responses to hypoxia, with the lower power output and metabolic rate in hypoxic TTs primarily regulated by reduced estimated glycogen oxidation. image Key points Substrate utilisation during exercise is affected by altitude, sex, training status, food intake and relative intensity. Whether sex‐ and altitude‐related differences in substrate utilisation persist during an ecologically valid maximal time trial in the fed state in trained males and females is unknown. Acute hypobaric hypoxia (∼2800 m) decreased 30 min time trial performance compared to normoxia (∼400 m) in both sexes, with a larger decrement in males. Females completed the time trials at a higher relative intensity than males in normoxia and hypoxia. Hypoxia reduced total metabolic rate primarily by decreasing estimated muscle glycogen oxidation, with no change in fat or blood glucose oxidation. The resulting changes in substrate partitioning were similar between sexes. Across altitudes, females derived relatively more energy from blood glucose despite similar muscle glycogen utilisation between sexes, whereas uncertain estimates suggested a lower contribution of fat in females than in males.

The resulting changes in substrate partitioning were similar between sexes. Across altitudes, females derived relatively more energy from blood glucose despite similar muscle glycogen utilisation between sexes, whereas uncertain estimates suggested a lower contribution of fat in females than in males.

papers.title: Effects of Packaging-Relevant Contaminants on the Property Evolution and Reprocessability of PET During Repeated Mechanical Recycling
papers.abstract: Residual polymeric contaminants from labels, closures, and adhesives can affect the quality and reprocessability of mechanically recycled polyethylene terephthalate (PET). Direct comparison of individual contaminants, however, is often complicated by differences in PET feedstock, contaminant concentration, and processing conditions among published studies. In this work, eight packaging-relevant contaminants—polypropylene (PP), low-density polyethylene (LDPE), high-density polyethylene (HDPE), polystyrene (PS), glycol-modified PET (PETG), poly(lactic acid) (PLA), poly(vinyl chloride) (PVC), and a commercial hot-melt labeling adhesive (HMA)—were compared at a fixed model concentration of 3 wt.% in bottle-grade PET under identical thermomechanical processing conditions. Contaminant selection was supported by ATR-FTIR screening of commercial bottle labels. Melt flow rate, MFR-derived intrinsic viscosity, differential scanning calorimetry, tensile properties, and CIE L*a*b* color characteristics were evaluated over successive processing stages. PET/PP, PET/LDPE, PET/HDPE, PET/PS, and PET/PETG remained processable through three processing stages, whereas PET/PLA and PET/HMA could only be processed through the second stage, and PET/PVC lost stable strand-forming ability after initial compounding. Tg and Tm remained comparatively stable, while crystallization temperature and PET crystallinity showed contaminant- and processing-dependent changes. Elongation at break was generally more sensitive to contamination than tensile strength, and PVC produced the most pronounced discoloration. Industrial PET fractions collected at successive separation and washing/decontamination stages were evaluated as a complementary case study. Progressive purification was associated with improved MFR-derived IV, while TGA showed only minor differences among the fractions. The results demonstrate that contaminant identity strongly affects PET property evolution and reprocessability during repeated mechanical recycling.

papers.title: Limits to adaptation: Agroforestry buffers but does not offset climate change impacts on maize yields in Dodoma, Tanzania
papers.abstract: Abstract Agricultural productivity in the semi-arid region of central Tanzania is low and projected to further decrease due to climate change, exacerbating the already high levels of food insecurity among the rural population. Agroforestry is actively promoted in the region as an adaptation strategy due to its multiple biophysical and socio-economic benefits, but whether it can buffer future climate change impacts on maize yields has not yet been quantified. Previous modelling studies in central Tanzania focused either on maize monocropping or on agroforestry under current climate. Moreover, it remains unclear whether yield gains from agroforestry constitute genuine adaptation. Here, we show for the first time how a comprehensive evaluation framework can be used to disaggregate projected yield changes into four distinct indicators: climate change impact, agroforestry impact, agroforestry adaptation effect, and climate change impact with adaptation. The Agricultural Production Systems Simulator was used to simulate maize yields at six sites in Dodoma under current climate conditions and under a low- and a high-emission scenario (shared socio-economic pathways 1-2.6 and 5-8.5) for two periods centred on 2030 (2016–2045) and 2050 (2036–2065). Above-ground agroforestry effects were represented by 10% and 20% shading, associated temperature reductions, and tree litter input. Without adaptation, climate change is projected to reduce maize yields by 23–33%. Agroforestry increased yields under all climate conditions, and the agroforestry adaptation effect grew towards 2050, with 20% shade being most effective. However, the climate change impact with adaptation shows that agroforestry buffers but does not offset yield losses: under the high-emission scenario, yields remained below the baseline at both shade levels, with losses increasing towards 2050. These results demonstrate both the potential and the limits of agroforestry as an adaptation strategy in semi-arid Tanzania.

papers.title: Development and characterization of coconut shell-derived carboxymethyl cellulose and nanocellulose as potential proton-conducting polymer electrolytes
papers.abstract: The development of sustainable solid polymer electrolytes from agricultural waste offers an environmentally friendly alternative to conventional synthetic polymers for energy storage applications. In this study, cellulose and nanocellulose were extracted from coconut shell powder and chemically modified into carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) and carboxymethyl nanocellulose (CMNC), followed by complexation with NH 4 NO 3 through the solvent-casting method. Successful carboxymethylation was confirmed by 1 H and 13 C NMR, where three carboxyl carbon signals at 177.43, 179.61, and 180.96 ppm verified the incorporation of carboxymethyl groups without polymer degradation. ATR-FTIR analysis confirmed the removal of lignin and hemicellulose and the formation of carboxylate groups. FESEM analysis revealed the morphology of coconut shell powder and cellulose. TEM analysis confirmed the nanoscale morphology of nanocellulose, with 54.05% of the particles exhibiting a size distribution within the range of 0–100 nm. Thermogravimetric analysis showed that CMNC exhibited lower thermal stability and degraded at 190°C due to the formation of sulfated amorphous regions during acid hydrolysis. X-ray diffraction analysis demonstrated that carboxymethylation reduced the crystallinity index from 46.40% to 64.27% for cellulose and nanocellulose to 3.54% and 20.45% for CMC and CMNC, respectively. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy revealed that the CMC electrolyte achieved the highest ionic conductivity of 2.87 × 10 -1 S cm -1 at 30 wt% NH 4 NO 3 , whereas CMNC (2.07 × 10 -3 S cm -1 ) highlighted its potential as a sustainable proton-conducting electrolyte for proton battery applications.

papers.title: METTL3-mediated m 6 A modification of DNMT1 enhances ovarian cancer progression
papers.abstract: Abstract High-grade serous carcinoma (HGSC), the most lethal subtype of ovarian cancer, is often diagnosed at advanced stages owing to its asymptomatic progression and lack of early detection markers. In this study, we identified a critical oncogenic role of the RNA methyltransferase METTL3 and the N 6 -methyladenosine (m 6 A) RNA modification pathway in HGSC. Depletion of METTL3 or its binding partner METTL14 impairs ovarian cancer proliferation and tumor progression. Mechanistically, m 6 A deposition enhances the translation of DNA methyltransferase DNMT1, an epigenetic repressor that silences tumor suppressor genes. Pharmacologic inhibition of DNMT1 led to DNA hypomethylation and upregulation of the tumor suppressors TNFAIP3 and FBXO32. Consistently, METTL3 depletion also increased the expression of these genes supporting a model in which METTL3 sustains oncogenesis by maintaining DNMT1 protein levels and repressing anti-tumor pathways. These findings position METTL3-mediated RNA modifications and DNMT1 as promising therapeutic targets in HGSC.

papers.title: Direct RNA sequencing reveals multi-layered regulation of the aging transcriptome
papers.abstract: Abstract BACKGROUND: Aging involves complex molecular alterations across tissues; however, a comprehensive understanding of epitranscriptomic dynamics remains elusive. RESULTS: Here, leveraging high-quality dRNA-seq, we simultaneously constructed a multi-tissue (lung, skeletal muscle, heart, and hippocampus), cross-species (mouse and human) dynamics atlas of RNA features during aging, namely N 6-methyladenosine (m 6 A), 5-methylcytidine (m 5 C), pseudouridine (Ψ), inosine, alternative polyadenylation (APA), and splicing. Our analysis revealed widespread non-linear, age-dependent shifts across these RNA features, exhibiting both conserved patterns and striking tissue specificity. Strikingly, a pronounced, transient peak in these shift events of RNA features occurred at mid-life (12 months of age in mice, 46 years of age in human), and affected the expression of aging-related, mitochondrial, and metabolic genes. CONCLUSIONS: Collectively, we present a high-resolution atlas of m 6 A, m 5 C, pseudouridine and inosine modifications, alternative splicing and poly(A) site usage across tissues and aging stages, derived from direct RNA sequencing. This resource offers an unprecedented foundation for dissecting the RNA-centric mechanisms that govern mammalian aging.

papers.title: Enhanced sampling enables binding site water reorganization in polarizable absolute binding free energy calculations
papers.abstract: Abstract Water molecules play a critical role in mediating protein-ligand interactions by forming hydrogen-bonding networks and contributing to ligand solvation. However, their behavior—ranging from rapid solvent exchange to persistent occupancy of buried sites—makes accurate binding free-energy estimation with molecular dynamics challenging. Inadequate sampling of water reorganization can bias computed affinities and obscure key interactions by preventing representative hydration states during calculations. To address this, we employ the polarizable AMOEBA force field together with Lambda-ABF-OPES, an integrated enhanced-sampling framework combining lambda-dynamics, multiple-walker adaptive biasing force, and on-the-fly probability enhanced sampling. AMOEBA provides a polarizable description of protein–ligand, ligand–water, and protein–water interactions, while the dynamic alchemical coordinate and adaptive biasing facilitate exploration of coupled ligand-pocket-solvent configurations during ligand decoupling. This construction allows water exchange, binding-site rehydration and solvent reorganization to emerge along the alchemical pathway without explicitly biasing water-based collective variables. Applied to five protein-ligand complexes spanning buried and semi-buried environments, the approach yields binding affinities in good agreement with experiment and captures relevant water-mediated reorganization to provide reproducible absolute binding free energies.

papers.title: From the Rock Floor to the Cloud: A Systematic Review of State-of-the-Art NLP in Battery Life Cycle
papers.abstract: This work presents a systematic review of the application of natural language processing (NLP) along the entire battery life cycle, instead of reviewing one stage or method, and introduces a novel conceptual technical language processing (TLP) framework for the European Union (EU)’s proposed digital battery passport (DBP) and other general battery predictions, as the main objective. It follows the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) method and employs three reputable databases or search engines, including Google Scholar, Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers Xplore (IEEE Xplore), and Scopus, searched in October, 2025. The search criteria are ’text’, ’language processing’, and ’battery’, while the exclusion criteria are non-relevant papers and those published before 2017, which were applied to all databases, except IEEE Xplore because it turned up fewer results. Consequently, it assesses 274 scientific papers before the critical review of the final 66 relevant papers. We publicly provide artifacts of the review for validation and possible reproducibility. The findings show that new NLP tasks are emerging in the battery domain, which facilitate materials discovery and other stages of the life cycle. Notwithstanding, challenges remain, such as the lack of standard benchmarks. The proposed TLP framework, which incorporates agentic AI and optimized prompts, may be apt for tackling some of the challenges.

papers.title: Quantum algorithms for photoreactivity in cancer-targeted photosensitizers
papers.abstract: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) is a targeted cancer treatment that uses light-activated photosensitizers to generate reactive oxygen species that selectively destroy tumor cells, generally causing less collateral damage than conventional treatments. However, its clinical success hinges on the availability of photosensitizers with strong optical sensitivity and high efficiency in generating reactive oxygen species. While classical computational methods have provided useful insights into photosensitizer design, they struggle to scale and often lack the accuracy needed for these simulations. In this work, we show how fault-tolerant quantum algorithms can be used to identify promising photosensitizer candidates for PDT. To predict photosensitizer performance, we assess two computational properties. First, we quantify light sensitivity by calculating the cumulative absorption in the therapeutic window with a threshold projection algorithm. Second, we determine the efficiency of reactive oxygen generation by estimating intersystem crossing (ISC) rates using the evolution-proxy approach, complemented by a vibronic dynamic treatment where appropriate. We apply these algorithms to a clinically relevant and actively pursued class of photosensitizers, BODIPY derivatives, including heavy-atom and transition-metal-substituted systems that are challenging for classical methods. Our resource estimates, obtained with PennyLane, suggest that systems with active spaces ranging from 11 to 45 spatial orbitals can be simulated using $180$-$350$ logical qubits and Toffoli gate depths between $10^7$ and $10^9$, placing our algorithms within reach of realistic fault-tolerant quantum devices. This paves the way to an efficient quantum-based workflow for designing photosensitizers that can accelerate the discovery of new PDT agents.

papers.title: Adversarial robustness of deep learning-based thyroid nodule segmentation in ultrasound
papers.abstract: Deep learning-based segmentation models are increasingly integrated into clinical imaging workflows, yet their robustness to adversarial perturbations remains incompletely characterized, particularly for ultrasound images. We evaluated adversarial attacks and inference-time defenses for thyroid nodule segmentation in B-mode ultrasound. Two black-box adversarial attacks were developed: (1) Structured Speckle Amplification Attack (SSAA), which injects boundary-targeted noise, and (2) Frequency-Domain Ultrasound Attack (FDUA), which applies bandpass-filtered phase perturbations in the Fourier domain. Three inference-time mitigations were evaluated on adversarial images: randomized preprocessing with test-time augmentation, deterministic input denoising, and stochastic ensemble inference with consistency-aware aggregation. Experiments were conducted on a U-Net segmentation model trained on cine-clips from a database of 192 thyroid nodules. The baseline model achieved a mean Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) of 0.76 (SD 0.20) on unperturbed images. SSAA reduced DSC by 0.29 (SD 0.20), from 0.76 to 0.47, while maintaining high visual similarity (SSIM = 0.94). FDUA resulted in a smaller DSC reduction of 0.11 (SD 0.09), from 0.76 to 0.65, with lower visual fidelity (SSIM = 0.82). Against SSAA, all three defenses significantly improved DSC after correction, with deterministic denoising showing the largest recovery (+0.10, p < 0.001), followed by randomized preprocessing (+0.09, p < 0.001), and stochastic ensemble inference (+0.08, p = 0.002). No defense achieved statistically significant improvement against FDUA, although recall consistently improved at the cost of reduced precision. The tested inference-time defenses therefore partially mitigated spatial-domain perturbations, whereas statistically significant DSC recovery was not demonstrated against frequency-domain perturbations, highlighting attack-specific challenges in adversarial robustness evaluation.

papers.title: Distributed elasticity: a high-reward, moderate-risk strategy for efficient control modulation in insect flight
papers.journal: Journal of The Royal Society Interface
papers.abstract: The environments inhabited by flying insects demand a balance between flight efficiency and flight manoeuvrability. In structural oscillators such as the insect indirect flight motor, efficiency (arising from resonance) and manoeuvrability (arising from kinematic modulation) are typically quid pro quo, with modulation incurring penalties to efficiency. Band-type resonance is a phenomenon that offers, in theory, a strategy to lessen these penalties via careful navigation through a band of efficient kinematic states. However, identifying this band is challenging: no methods exist to identify the complete band in realistic motor models, involving elasticity distributed across thorax and wing. Nor are the effects of elasticity distribution on the band known. In this work, we address both open topics. We present a suite of numerical methods for identifying the complete resonance band in general systems. Applying them to models of the insect flight motor with distributed elasticity-thoracic and wing flexion-reveals that distributed elasticity is moderate-risk, but high-reward, morphological feature. Well-tuned distributions expand the resonance band over fourfold, whereas poorly tuned distributions completely extinguish the resonance band. These results indicate that distributing elasticity across the insect flight motor can have an adaptive value, and they motivate broader work identifying distributions across species.

papers.title: Squeezing and measurement of a mechanical quadrature via proportional-integral-derivative feedback
papers.abstract: Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) control is used for automatically regulating a measurable quantity to a desired setpoint. It is widely used in different types of classical control electronics. Here, we show how extending the feedback theory in quantum systems to include the derivative and integral parts influences both the transient and steady-state behavior of the amplitude and squeezing of a mechanical quadrature in an optomechanical system. We show that, in contrast to standard proportional feedback, derivative feedback affects both the conditional and unconditional squeezing. Furthermore, we demonstrate how feedback may be employed to drive a mechanical quadrature to track a desired reference signal. Our findings offer new routes for an improved quantum state control and measurement precision.

papers.title: Anisotropic response in bilayer graphene for light dark matter detection
papers.abstract: Novel target materials with anisotropic response will play a key role in detecting low-mass dark matter in upcoming experiments. Bilayer graphene is one such material that has been proposed for the detection of sub-MeV mass dark matter particles via electronic excitations. In this work, we calculate scattering rate via a massive mediator in bilayer graphene. With an exposure as small as $\sim$ 0.5 mg-year, bilayer graphene can probe new regions of the parameter space. The anisotropic response function of bilayer graphene leads to a sidereal-day modulation in the scattering rate, depending on its orientation with respect to the Galactic dark matter wind. We find significant modulation in the scattering rate for sub-MeV mass dark matter, demonstrating bilayer graphene's promise for a future experiment. We hope that our work will motivate the community to investigate bilayer graphene as a novel target material, and that it may lead us to discover the particle nature of dark matter.

papers.title: Unraveling Mechanistic Pathways and Selectivity Patterns in Visible-Light-Driven Aliphatic C–H Functionalization with a Carbon Nitride Photocatalyst
papers.abstract: Abstract Visible-light-driven heterogeneous photocatalysis based on carbon nitride materials has recently emerged as a sustainable platform for aliphatic C–H functionalization, although key mechanistic aspects and selectivity factors remain poorly understood. Herein, we report a combined experimental and computational investigation wherein mesoporous graphitic carbon nitride (mpg-CN) has been exploited in Giese-type C–H functionalization reactions of diverse aliphatic substrates. Under mild and additive-free conditions, mpg-CN enabled the redox-neutral formation of C–C bonds with electron-poor olefins, displaying a reactivity profile strongly dependent on substrate structure. Mechanistic studies, supported by density functional theory calculations, reveal that C–H bond cleavage proceeds via a proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) pathway. A correlation between bond dissociation free energies and functionalization yield has been identified, establishing a thermodynamic threshold for reactivity. Furthermore, adsorption of substrates within the catalyst surface grooves emerges as a key factor dictating both reactivity and site selectivity, when applicable. In particular, steric constraints and substrate–surface interactions govern accessibility to reactive sites, leading to distinctive selectivity patterns compared to homogeneous photocatalysts, notably the decatungstate anion. These findings highlight the unique role of heterogeneous catalysts in guiding the outcome of photocatalytic processes and provide fundamental insights for the rational design of selective carbon nitride-based synthetic transformations.

papers.title: Anomalous thermal and elastic properties of an epitaxial NiTi film exhibiting R-phase
papers.abstract: Abstract Shape memory alloys like NiTi are at the core of emerging thermal management applications, including elastocaloric refrigeration, thermoelastic harvesting, and latent heat storage. Most of these applications benefit from a small scale due to the accelerated heat exchange, but obtaining precise functional properties of films is challenging. Here we demonstrate that transient grating spectroscopy (TGS) enables characterization of elastic coefficients and thermal diffusivity of a 3 µm thick epitaxial NiTi film during a thermally induced phase transformation. The in-situ measurement of a complete austenite→R-phase→martensite→austenite temperature cycle reveals that the elastic properties exhibit a crossover of the shear moduli (from c ′ < c 44 in austenite to c ′ > c 44 in martensite) and that the thermal diffusivity changes by a factor of 4.5 between the R-phase and austenite. This dramatic change, together with the absence of hysteresis between the R-phase and austenite, makes NiTi a promising material candidate for thermal switches. The results indicate that the change in thermal diffusivity originates from an anomalous heat capacity of the R-phase. Furthermore, our TGS study provides temperature-dependent thermal and elastic properties required for simulating thermal management microsystems using this material.

papers.journal: The European Physical Journal Special Topics
papers.abstract: Abstract The Compressed Baryonic Matter (CBM) fixed-target experiment is under construction at the Facility for Antiproton and Ion Research. It aims to explore the phase structure of strong interaction (QCD) matter at high net-baryon densities and moderate temperatures using heavy-ion collisions in the center-of-mass energy range per nucleon pair $$\sqrt{s_{\textrm{NN}}} =$$ s NN = 2.7–4.9 GeV. Equipped with fast and radiation-hard detector systems and an advanced triggerless data acquisition scheme, CBM will collect data at interaction rates of up to 10 MHz by performing online reconstruction and event selection. This will facilitate measurements of rare probes not accessible so far in this energy range, including multi-strange hadron production and their flow coefficients, high-order net-baryon cumulants, dileptons, as well as production of double-strange hypernuclei. The CBM detector is outlined and selected physics performance results based on realistic simulations are discussed.

papers.title: Stablecoin depegging, financial intermediary balance sheet constraints, and liquidity in the U.S. traditional money market
papers.abstract: Abstract As the stablecoin market has expanded rapidly, its links with the U.S. traditional money market have become increasingly close. This paper examines the dynamic effects of stablecoin depegging on U.S. money market liquidity. We develop an analytical framework incorporating stablecoins and show that depegging transmits liquidity stress by tightening financial intermediaries’ balance sheet constraints. Using local projections, we find marked heterogeneity across markets: Treasury bill liquidity improves initially before reversing, commercial paper liquidity deteriorates on the shock day, and repo market liquidity worsens with a delayed peak. Further analysis shows that these effects operate mainly through a higher marginal cost of expanding balance sheet capacity, rather than a large capital drawdown. When intermediary capital is under stress, liquidity deterioration is significantly amplified across all three markets. These findings document risk coupling between crypto-asset markets and traditional money markets and offer policy implications for macroprudential stablecoin regulation.

papers.title: Tunable signal penetration and response plateaus in bistable mechanical media
papers.abstract: Dynamically processing mechanical signals is crucial for soft robotics and mechanosensing, where classical viscoelastic materials lack intrinsic tunability. We show that internal bistability actively controls the response and signal attenuation in mechanical (meta)materials. In our model, bistable elements switch discretely with a predefined timescale between states distinguished by potential energy $ε$, equilibrium length $Δl$, and spring constant $Δk$. The system is simulated via microscopic Brownian dynamics coupled to Poisson switching with rate $ν$, and described macroscopically by a nonlinear continuum field theory. Crucially, the model yields closed-form analytical solutions for the linear response and spatial penetration depth, revealing two phenomena: a universal screening mechanism (akin to the electrostatic 'skin effect') reducing spatial signal penetration when the driving frequency exceeds the internal relaxation rate, and a frequency-insensitive response plateau from timescale separation. The screening length is controlled primarily by the conformational length change $Δl$, while the attenuation regime and plateau are tuneable via the switching rate $ν$. A systematic parameter study exposes a fundamental design trade-off: larger $Δl$ strengthens dissipation but raises the energy barrier for state transitions, eventually causing state-locking where damping vanishes. Optimal attenuation thus requires a compromise between pronounced bistability and a surmountable barrier. Due to its analytical tractability, our framework provides explicit design rules for fine-tuning the adaptive response of bistable media. It applies to diverse experimental systems-from biopolymers to synthetic catch bonds and metamaterials-enabling the predictive engineering of intelligent soft matter for frequency-selective signal processing.

papers.title: Dynamical quantum phase transitions in a pseudo-Hermitian Hamiltonian: The imbalanced-pairing Kitaev model
papers.abstract: Although parity-time (PT)-symmetric Hamiltonians are often associated with real energy spectra, PT symmetry is neither a sufficient nor a necessary condition for a real spectrum. More generally, real spectra are associated with the broader class of pseudo-Hermitian Hamiltonians, of which PT-symmetric Hamiltonians constitute a simple subclass. Here, we investigate the nonequilibrium dynamics of the imbalanced-pairing Kitaev model, a prototypical pseudo-Hermitian system, under a linearly time-dependent chemical potential. The dynamics are analyzed within the biorthogonal framework using the concept of dynamical quantum phase transitions (DQPTs). We show that, under a linear ramp protocol, DQPTs occur only when the post-ramp Hamiltonian possesses a real energy spectrum. For positive values of the non-Hermiticity parameter ($γ>0$), where the energy spectrum remains entirely real, a ramp crossing a single quantum critical point gives rise to a single family of critical times, analogous to the Hermitian case. Furthermore, for ramps crossing two critical or exceptional points, the critical sweep velocity above which DQPTs disappear decreases as the non-Hermiticity parameter is reduced and vanishes in the staggered-pairing limit, $γ=-1$.

papers.title: End-of-Life Management of Photovoltaic Modules: Recycling, Second-Life Applications, and Disposal
papers.abstract: The rapid global expansion of photovoltaic (PV) systems, driven by rising energy demand, is expected to generate substantial module waste at end-of-life, with global PV waste projected to exceed 4 million tonnes by 2030, 50 million by 2040, and 200 million tonnes by 2050. Based on 102 publications identified through Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and IEEE Xplore databases, this review provides a comparative, literature-based assessment of recycling, second-life applications, and disposal as end-of-life (EoL) management strategies for PV modules, examining the relationship between module structure, waste management pathways, material recovery potential, and the technical and economic limitations of current practices. Recycling offers clear environmental benefits but remains economically constrained in many scenarios by high process costs and the complexity of separating laminated module structures. Second-life application emerges as a complementary strategy, delaying the premature entry of modules retaining residual functionality into the waste stream and enhancing resource efficiency. Nevertheless, landfilling continues to account for the majority of global PV waste despite the availability of more sustainable alternatives, revealing a marked gap between technical potential and field-level practice. Overall, no single approach is sufficient; effective PV waste management requires an integrated strategy combining recycling, second-life applications, and disposal in line with circular economy principles.

papers.title: Adaptive Discovery of Uncharted Zeolitic Imidazolate Frameworks
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract: Abstract Discovering new zeolitic imidazolate framework (ZIF) structures remains a major challenge because their assembly depends on the nature of the linker and synthesis conditions. Here, we introduce linker width as a design parameter for ZIF synthesis. We designed 4-substituted benzimidazole linkers with expanded width and combined them with smaller linkers in an adaptive machine-learning (ML) high-throughput strategy. This adaptive discovery scheme yielded nine new mixed-linker ZIFs, including six adopting the previously unrealized bcv topology. Single-crystal structural analysis reveals ordered linker distributions in which the wider 4-substituted benzimidazolate linkers code for the formation of 10-membered-ring needed for the apertures of the bcv cage. Comparison with representative mixed-linker ZIFs further identifies the width of linkers and the extension ratio as steric descriptors of topology selection. These results provide chemically interpretable design principles for mixed-linker ZIF assembly and demonstrate how linker design coupled with ML-guided synthesis can access unexplored regions of chemical space.

papers.title: Comparative Effects of Soxhlet Extraction and Thermal Treatment on the Physicochemical Properties of Spent Bleaching Earth for Sustainable Reuse
papers.abstract: Abstract This study evaluates the effects of solvent extraction and thermal treatment on the structural, mineralogical, and physicochemical properties of spent bleaching earth (SBE) from a palm oil refinery, aimed at sustainable reuse strategies. The SBE was subjected to Soxhlet extraction using n-hexane, as well as another process through calcination between 300 and 1000°C. Products were characterized by XRF, XRD, TGA/DSC, laser granulometry, SEM/EDS, and FTIR. The raw industrial bentonitic material exhibited a typical aluminosilicate composition: montmorillonite, illite, and kaolinite. Solvent extraction virtually removed residual oil from the bleaching process of palm oil, without significant changes in chemical composition or crystalline structure, preserving lamellar morphology, although with an increase in amorphous content. In contrast, thermal treatment promoted transformations, including structural collapse of montmorillonite, dehydroxylation of clay minerals, and formation of thermally stable phases, as well as particle agglomeration. Thermal analysis along with chemical extraction indicated approximately 25 wt.% residual oil content, and mass loss of about 40 wt.% from volatile materials. Results show that solvent extraction favors partial reactivation for adsorptive applications, whereas calcination produces a structurally modified material with potential for ceramic applications, possibly contributing to circular economy practices in vegetable oil refining.

papers.title: Remote Adiabatic Controlled-Z Gate between Distant Superconducting Qubits
papers.abstract: Abstract Direct entangling gates between spatially separated qubits are a key capability for modular quantum computing. They enable nonlocal quantum circuits to be executed across different processor modules, thereby alleviating single-chip scaling constraints and expanding the effective connectivity of the system. Here, we propose and numerically investigate a remote adiabatic controlled-Z gate between two frequency-tunable superconducting qubits connected by a multi-mode coaxial cable. The cable-mediated interaction enables the gate to be implemented without additional tunable couplers, preserving a simple circuit architecture. For a 30-cm cable, simulations incorporating ten standing-wave modes yield a gate infidelity of 4.71×10 -7 with a duration of 376.7 ns in the absence of decoherence. When qubit decoherence and cable loss are included, the gate infidelity is 6.37×10 -3 for representative coherence parameters. Moreover, the gate maintains high fidelity under qubit-frequency fluctuations and millimeter-scale cable-length variations. Calculations for 50- and 100-cm cable situations demonstrate its potential for even larger cryogenic systems. These results provide a promising approach to extending high-fidelity quantum operations beyond individual chips and toward scalable, interconnected superconducting quantum processors.

papers.title: An experimental study of expanding spherical laminar lean H2/O2/N2/He flames
papers.abstract: Experiments with confined spherical laminar flames expanding in lean (the equivalence ratio ϕ = 0.45) H 2 /O 2 /N 2 /He mixtures under room conditions are performed using high-speed Schlieren technique. Measured dependencies of (i) flame radius on time and (ii) flame speed on flame stretch rate are analyzed using four state-of-the-art methods. The following results are worth emphasizing. First, at large ratios of mole fractions X He and X N 2 of He and N 2 , respectively, e.g., X He / X N 2 = 1.81 , no visible cellularity was observed within the investigated flame radius range. Second, experimental data obtained at X He / X N 2 = 0.51 or 0.45 indicate that both (i) cells on flame surface and (ii) an increase in the flame speed due to flame instability appear at sufficiently large flame radii, more than 7 ms after the end of the spark discharge. This experimental finding is consistent with the standpoint that high stretch rates can suppress diffusional-thermal and Darrieus-Landau instabilities. Third, the performed measurements demonstrate that changing He:N 2 ratio in lean H 2 /O 2 /N 2 /He mixtures offers the opportunity to explore onset of cellular instability by separating it from ignition stage. Fourth, the experiments also show that although the truncation of the data obtained at large flame radii offers the opportunity to explore apparently stable flames in the case of a negative Markstein number M a b , such a method results in fitting-dependent and scattered values of laminar flame speeds and, especially, M a b .
